136	def _sent(led) -> dict[str, dict]:
137	    """Latest pushed-or-seeded record per key (both mean the receiver has that content)."""
138	    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
139	    for r in led.records():
140	        if r["event"] in ("pushed", "seeded") and r.get("key"):
141	            out[r["key"]] = r
142	    return out
143	
144	
145	def _candidates(job: Job, led, stage: Path, first_pass: bool, inventory: dict[str, str],
146	                log):
147	    """Units to pack now: new, or changed since last sent; seeded ones are recorded."""
148	    sent = _sent(led)
149	    units = enumerate_units(job.units)
150	    recheck = None
151	    if not first_pass and job.units.recheck_recent:
152	        recheck = {u.key for u in units[-job.units.recheck_recent:]}
153	    now = time.time()
154	    for unit in units:
155	        prev = sent.get(unit.key)
156	        if (stage / unit.key / "manifest.json").exists():
157	            continue
158	        if prev and (not job.units.resend_changed or job.sender.delete_source != "never"
159	                     or (recheck is not None and unit.key not in recheck)):
160	            continue
161	        fp = fingerprint(unit)
162	        if fp.files == 0:
163	            continue
164	        if prev and prev.get("fingerprint") == fp.digest:
165	            continue
166	        if job.units.settle_seconds and now - fp.newest_mtime < job.units.settle_seconds:
167	            log.info("%s still settling (newest file %.0fs old)", unit.key, now - fp.newest_mtime)
168	            continue
169	        if not prev and inventory.get(unit.key) == fp.digest:
170	            led.append("seeded", unit.key, fingerprint=fp.digest, size=fp.bytes, files=fp.files,
171	                       revision=1)
172	            continue
173	        if prev:
174	            log.info("%s changed since revision %d; re-sending", unit.key,
175	                     prev.get("revision", 1))
176	        yield unit, fp, (prev.get("revision", 1) + 1) if prev else 1
177	
178	
179	def _read_inventory(job: Job, adapter, led, log) -> dict[str, str]:
180	    text = adapter.get_text(inventory_path(job.remote.prefix), job.state_dir / "scratch")
181	    if not text:
182	        return {}
183	    data = json.loads(text)
184	    seen = {r.get("created_at") for r in led.records() if r["event"] == "inventory"}
185	    if data.get("created_at") not in seen:
186	        led.append("inventory", created_at=data.get("created_at"), units=len(data["keys"]))
187	        log.info("receiver inventory with %d units (%s)", len(data["keys"]),
188	                 data.get("created_at"))
189	    return data["keys"]
190	
191	
192	def _wait_pack_slot(job: Job, stage: Path, stop: threading.Event, log) -> None:
193	    announced = False
194	    while not stop.is_set():
195	        wait = blocked_for(list(job.sender.read_blocked))
196	        if wait <= 0 and job.sender.stage_cap and staged(stage) and \
197	                dir_bytes(stage) >= job.sender.stage_cap:
198	            wait = 30
199	        if wait <= 0:
200	            return
201	        if not announced:
202	            log.info("packing paused for %ds (read window or staging cap)", wait)
203	            announced = True
204	        stop.wait(min(wait, 300))
205	
206	
207	def _remote_inflight(job: Job, adapter, led) -> int:
208	    pushed = led.keys("pushed")
209	    keys = [e.rstrip("/") for e in adapter.list(job.remote.prefix)
210	            if e.endswith("/") and not e.startswith("_")]
211	    return sum(pushed[k]["size"] for k in keys if k in pushed)
212	
213	
214	def _push_unit(job: Job, adapter, directory: Path, led, log, stop, poll) -> bool:
215	    manifest = Manifest.from_json((directory / "manifest.json").read_text())
216	    key = manifest.key
217	    free = adapter.free_bytes()
218	    if free is not None and free - manifest.size < job.remote.min_free:
219	        log.info("remote free %d bytes below floor; waiting before %s", free, key)
220	        stop.wait(poll)
221	        return False
222	    if job.remote.max_inflight and \
223	            _remote_inflight(job, adapter, led) + manifest.size > job.remote.max_inflight:
224	        log.info("remote in-flight limit reached; waiting before %s", key)
225	        stop.wait(poll)
226	        return False
227	    remote = unit_dir(job.remote.prefix, key)
228	    started = time.monotonic()
229	    for part in manifest.parts:
230	        target = f"{remote}/{part.name}"
231	        if adapter.stat(target) == part.size:
232	            continue  # uploaded before a restart
233	        adapter.put(directory / part.name, target)
234	        got = adapter.stat(target)
235	        if got != part.size:
236	            raise RuntimeError(f"{target}: remote size {got} != local {part.size}")
237	    adapter.put(directory / "manifest.json", f"{remote}/manifest.json")
238	    if adapter.stat(f"{remote}/manifest.json") is None:
239	        raise RuntimeError(f"{remote}/manifest.json missing after upload")
240	    secs = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
241	    info = json.loads((directory / "unit.json").read_text())
242	    led.append("pushed", key, size=manifest.size, sha256=manifest.sha256, secs=secs,
243	               root=info["root"], members=info["members"],
244	               fingerprint=info.get("fingerprint", ""), revision=info.get("revision", 1))
245	    log.info("pushed %s %d bytes in %.0fs (%.1f MB/s)", key, manifest.size, secs,
246	             manifest.size / 1e6 / max(secs, 1e-3))
247	    if job.sender.delete_source == "after_remote_size":
248	        _delete_source(key, info, led, log)
249	    shutil.rmtree(directory)
250	    return True
251	
252	
253	def _delete_source(key: str, info: dict, led, log) -> None:
254	    root = Path(info["root"])
255	    for member in info["members"]:
256	        remove_inside(root, member)
257	    led.append("source_deleted", key)
258	    log.info("deleted source of %s", key)
259	
260	
261	def _awaiting_acks(led) -> bool:
262	    return bool(set(led.keys("pushed")) - set(led.keys("source_deleted")))
263	
264	
265	def _consume_acks(job: Job, adapter, led, log) -> None:
266	    pushed, deleted = led.keys("pushed"), led.keys("source_deleted")
267	    for entry in adapter.list(f"{job.remote.prefix}/_acks"):
268	        key = entry.removesuffix(".json")
269	        if key in pushed and key not in deleted:
270	            _delete_source(key, pushed[key], led, log)
271	        if key in pushed:
272	            adapter.delete(ack_path(job.remote.prefix, key))

2	
3	A unit is READY when its ``manifest.json`` exists remotely. Each part is checked against
4	the manifest's size and sha256 before reassembly; the reassembled payload is checked
5	against the whole-stream sha256 and, for tars, the member count. Only then is the
6	relay copy deleted. Already-verified parts are kept across restarts.

24	READ_BUF = 8 << 20

27	@dataclass

38	def receive(job: Job, *, once: bool = False, follow: bool = False, allow_proxy: bool = False,

48	        require(preflight(job, adapter, allow_proxy=allow_proxy), log)
49	        led = ledger(job, "receiver")
50	        led.append("start", once=once, follow=follow, allow_proxy=allow_proxy)
51	        attempts: dict[str, int] = {}
52	        while not stop.is_set():
53	            entries = adapter.list(job.remote.prefix)
54	            keys = sorted(e.rstrip("/") for e in entries
55	                          if e.endswith("/") and not e.startswith("_"))
56	            verified = led.keys("verified")
57	            progressed = False
58	            for key in keys:
59	                if stop.is_set():
60	                    break
61	                text = adapter.get_text(f"{unit_dir(job.remote.prefix, key)}/manifest.json",
62	                                        scratch)
63	                if text is None:
64	                    continue  # still uploading
65	                try:
66	                    manifest = Manifest.from_json(text)
67	                    if verified.get(key, {}).get("sha256") == manifest.sha256:
68	                        # verified earlier; only the relay cleanup did not finish
69	                        adapter.delete(unit_dir(job.remote.prefix, key))
70	                        continue
71	                    if not _has_room(job, manifest, log):
72	                        break
73	                    _receive_unit(job, adapter, manifest, led, log)
74	                    progressed = True
75	                except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep receiving other units
76	                    attempts[key] = attempts.get(key, 0) + 1
77	                    log.error("receive %s failed (attempt %d): %s", key, attempts[key], e)
78	                    led.append("failed", key, error=str(e)[:500], attempt=attempts[key])
79	                    if key not in failed:
80	                        failed.append(key)
81	            if once:
82	                break
83	            if not follow and not progressed and \
84	                    adapter.stat(sender_done_path(job.remote.prefix)) is not None and \
85	                    not any(e.endswith("/") and not e.startswith("_")
86	                            for e in adapter.list(job.remote.prefix)):
87	                log.info("sender finished and relay is empty; receiver done")
88	                break
89	            if not progressed:
90	                stop.wait(poll)
91	        done = led.keys("verified")
92	        led.append("stop")
93	        return ReceiveResult(verified=len(done), failed=[k for k in failed if k not in done],
94	                             verified_bytes=sum(r["size"] for r in done.values()))
95	
96	
97	def _has_room(job: Job, m: Manifest, log) -> bool:
98	    assert job.receiver is not None
99	    dest = dest_dir(job.receiver, m.key)
100	    probe = dest
101	    while not probe.exists() and probe != probe.parent:
102	        probe = probe.parent
103	    free = shutil.disk_usage(probe).free
104	    need = job.receiver.min_free + 2 * m.size
105	    if free < need:
106	        log.warning("destination free %d bytes < %d needed for %s; waiting", free, need, m.key)
107	        return False
108	    return True
109	
110	
111	def _extract_replacing(archive: Path, dest: Path, m: Manifest) -> None:
112	    """Extract so that each unit path mirrors the sender exactly (stale files removed).
113	
114	    Paths are swapped one by one: extract into a scratch dir on the same filesystem, move
115	    the current copy aside, move the new one in, then drop the old copy.
116	    """
117	    scratch = dest / f".ferry-extract-{m.key}"
118	    old = dest / f".ferry-old-{m.key}"
119	    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
120	    shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True)
121	    scratch.mkdir(parents=True)
122	    with tarfile.open(archive, "r:") as tar:
123	        tar.extractall(scratch, filter="data")
124	    paths = m.paths or tuple(p.name for p in scratch.iterdir())
125	    for rel in paths:
126	        new, target = scratch / rel, dest / rel
127	        if not new.exists():
128	            continue
129	        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
130	        if target.exists() or target.is_symlink():
131	            (old / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
132	            os.replace(target, old / rel)
133	        os.replace(new, target)
134	    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
135	    shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True)
136	
137	
138	def _sha256(path: Path) -> str:
139	    h = hashlib.sha256()
140	    with path.open("rb") as f:
141	        while chunk := f.read(READ_BUF):
142	            h.update(chunk)
143	    return h.hexdigest()
144	
145	
146	def _receive_unit(job: Job, adapter, m: Manifest, led, log) -> None:
147	    assert job.receiver is not None
148	    dest = dest_dir(job.receiver, m.key)
149	    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
150	    final = dest / m.filename
151	    remote = unit_dir(job.remote.prefix, m.key)
152	    started = time.monotonic()
153	    if not (final.is_file() and final.stat().st_size == m.size and _sha256(final) == m.sha256):
154	        partial = dest / f".ferry-{m.key}.partial"
155	        partial.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
156	        for part in m.parts:
157	            local = partial / part.name
158	            if local.is_file() and local.stat().st_size == part.size and \
159	                    _sha256(local) == part.sha256:
160	                continue
161	            adapter.get(f"{remote}/{part.name}", local)
162	            if local.stat().st_size != part.size or _sha256(local) != part.sha256:
163	                local.unlink(missing_ok=True)
164	                raise VerifyError(f"{m.key}/{part.name}: size or sha256 mismatch")
165	        tmp = dest / f".{m.filename}.ferry-tmp"
166	        if len(m.parts) == 1:
167	            os.replace(partial / m.parts[0].name, tmp)
168	        else:
169	            h = hashlib.sha256()
170	            with tmp.open("wb") as out:
171	                for part in m.parts:
172	                    with (partial / part.name).open("rb") as f:
173	                        while chunk := f.read(READ_BUF):
174	                            out.write(chunk)
175	                            h.update(chunk)
176	            if h.hexdigest() != m.sha256:
177	                tmp.unlink()
178	                raise VerifyError(f"{m.key}: reassembled sha256 mismatch")
179	        if len(m.parts) == 1 and m.parts[0].sha256 != m.sha256:
180	            tmp.unlink()
181	            raise VerifyError(f"{m.key}: whole-payload sha256 mismatch")
182	        os.replace(tmp, final)
183	        shutil.rmtree(partial, ignore_errors=True)
184	    transfer_secs = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
185	    if m.format == "tar":
186	        with tarfile.open(final, "r:") as tar:
187	            members = sum(1 for t in tar if not t.isdir())
188	        if members != m.members:
189	            raise VerifyError(f"{m.key}: tar has {members} files, manifest says {m.members}")
190	        if job.receiver.extract:
191	            _extract_replacing(final, dest, m)
192	            final.unlink()
193	    led.append("verified", m.key, size=m.size, sha256=m.sha256, members=m.members,
194	               secs=transfer_secs, path=str(final), revision=m.revision,
195	               fingerprint=m.fingerprint)
196	    log.info("verified %s %d bytes in %.0fs (%.1f MB/s)", m.key, m.size, transfer_secs,
197	             m.size / 1e6 / max(transfer_secs, 1e-3))
198	    if m.ack_required:
199	        adapter.put_text(json.dumps({"key": m.key, "sha256": m.sha256, "at": utcnow()}),
200	                         ack_path(job.remote.prefix, m.key), job.state_dir / "scratch")
201	    adapter.delete(remote)
202	    led.append("remote_deleted", m.key)

19	    pass

26	@dataclass
27	class Preflight:
28	    adapter: str
29	    egress_policy: str
30	    problems: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # always fatal
31	    egress_findings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # fatal under "direct"
32	    routes: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
33	    proxy_env_stripped: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
34	
35	    @property
36	    def ok(self) -> bool:
37	        return not self.problems and (self.egress_policy == "any" or not self.egress_findings)
38	
39	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
40	        return {**asdict(self), "ok": self.ok}

43	def adapter_for(job: Job, side: str) -> Adapter:
44	    name, options = job.remote.for_side(side)
45	    return make_adapter(name, options, log=job.state_dir / f"{side}.transfer.log")

48	def preflight(job: Job, adapter: Adapter, *, allow_proxy: bool = False, routes=None) -> Preflight:
49	    policy = "any" if allow_proxy else job.remote.egress
50	    report = Preflight(adapter=adapter.name, egress_policy=policy,
51	                       proxy_env_stripped=proxy_vars_present())
52	    report.problems.extend(adapter.check())
53	    report.egress_findings.extend(adapter.proxy_settings())
54	    if routes is None:
55	        def routes(hosts):
56	            return check_routes(hosts, trusted=job.remote.trusted_interfaces)
57	    for finding in routes(adapter.endpoints):
58	        report.routes.append(asdict(finding))
59	        if finding.problem:
60	            report.egress_findings.append(f"{finding.host}: {finding.problem}")
61	    return report
62	
63	
64	def require(report: Preflight, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
65	    for item in report.egress_findings:
66	        log.warning("egress: %s", item)
67	    if report.proxy_env_stripped:
68	        log.info("proxy variables removed for child processes: %s",
69	                 ", ".join(report.proxy_env_stripped))
70	    if not report.ok:
71	        reasons = report.problems + (
72	            report.egress_findings if report.egress_policy == "direct" else [])
73	        raise PreflightError("preflight failed: " + "; ".join(reasons) + (
74	            "\n(egress findings can be accepted with remote.egress = \"any\" or --allow-proxy)"
75	            if report.egress_findings and report.egress_policy == "direct" else ""))

78	@contextmanager
79	def instance_lock(job: Job, side: str):
80	    """One sender and one receiver per job and host; a second instance fails fast."""
81	    job.state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
82	    path = job.state_dir / f"{side}.lock"
83	    fh = path.open("a+")
84	    try:
85	        fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
86	    except BlockingIOError:
87	        fh.seek(0)
88	        holder = fh.read().strip() or "?"
89	        fh.close()
90	        raise AlreadyRunning(f"another ferry {side} for job {job.name} is running "
91	                             f"(pid {holder}, lock {path})") from None
92	    fh.seek(0)
93	    fh.truncate()
94	    fh.write(str(os.getpid()))
95	    fh.flush()
96	    try:
97	        yield
98	    finally:
99	        fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
100	        fh.close()
101

103	def logger(job: Job, side: str) -> logging.Logger:
104	    log = logging.getLogger(f"ferry.{job.name}.{side}")
105	    if not log.handlers:
106	        job.state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
107	        fmt = logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
108	        for handler in (logging.FileHandler(job.state_dir / f"{side}.log"),
109	                        logging.StreamHandler()):
110	            handler.setFormatter(fmt)
111	            log.addHandler(handler)
112	        log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
113	        log.propagate = False
114	    return log

121	def remove_inside(root: Path, rel: str) -> None:
122	    """Delete root/rel, refusing anything that resolves outside root."""
123	    target = (root / rel)
124	    resolved = target.resolve()
125	    if not resolved.is_relative_to(root.resolve()) or resolved == root.resolve():
126	        raise PreflightError(f"refusing to delete {target}: outside source root")
127	    if target.is_dir() and not target.is_symlink():
128	        shutil.rmtree(target)
129	    else:
130	        target.unlink(missing_ok=True)

````text
1	# Operations
2	
3	## Inspect before transferring
4	
5	```sh
6	ferry doctor job.toml
7	ferry doctor job.toml --side receiver
8	ferry plan job.toml
9	ferry status job.toml
10	ferry status job.toml --side receiver --json
11	ferry status job.toml --scan-source --remote
12	```
13	
14	Doctor checks the selected backend and egress; it can contact remote services
15	and, for rsync, create a missing landing directory. It is not a generic dry-run
16	or proof that every later backend operation will succeed. Plan enumerates source
17	units and members; it does not simulate transfer, settling, or source deletion.
18	
19	Status normally reads local ledgers. `--scan-source` adds source enumeration;
20	`--remote` queries the backend for relay information. Sender and receiver have
21	separate state, so inspect each on its own host. Commands accept `--json`, but
22	service output remains supervisor text rather than a general JSON report.
23	
24	## Run and resume
25	
26	```sh
27	ferry send job.toml
28	ferry receive job.toml --once
29	```
30	
31	Send processes eligible work and marks the sender done. Receive with `--once`
32	makes one pass; without it, receive waits until the sender is done and the relay
33	is empty. For continuous operation, run `send --follow` and `receive --follow`
34	in separate processes, adding `--poll 60` to control idle polling in seconds.
35	
36	To resume, restart the same command with the same job, state, staging, and relay
37	prefix. Do not delete ledgers, staged manifests, or destination partial files to
38	"fix" an interrupted transfer. Uploaded parts with matching remote sizes can be
39	reused; downloaded parts are checked by SHA-256 before reuse. One sender and one
40	receiver may run per job on a host; a second instance of either side fails fast.
41	
42	Inspect `<state_dir>/sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`, and side logs when progress
43	stalls. Check read windows, settling, staging space, remote limits, destination
44	free space, and preflight errors. Keep credentials and session files out of reports.
45	
46	## Integrity and destination safety
47	
48	The sender hashes the packed payload and its parts. The receiver checks sizes,
49	part and whole-payload SHA-256 hashes, and tar member counts before recording
50	verification. It then removes that unit's relay data. With extraction enabled,
51	existing unit paths are replaced, including removal of files absent in the new copy.
52	
53	Change detection is weaker than transfer verification: its path-and-size
54	fingerprints miss same-size edits. `ferry inventory job.toml --no-upload --json`
55	previews fingerprints of an existing destination tree; omit `--no-upload` only
56	when you intend to publish them to the relay for sender-side skipping. Use
57	`--root PATH` for a source-shaped tree when `receiver.dest` contains a key template.
58	Inventory seeding is not a content-hash audit or evidence of a fresh transfer.
59	
60	## Source deletion
61	
62	- `never` is the default and the recommended starting point.
63	- `after_remote_size` deletes source members after upload size checks, **before
64	  destination SHA-256 verification**. Use only for independently recoverable data.
65	- `after_receiver_ack` waits for the receiver's verification acknowledgement.
66	  Keep the sender running or restart it to consume acknowledgements; one-shot
67	  sending can wait for the receiver rather than exiting immediately.
68	
69	Keep source units immutable throughout transfer and acknowledgement handling:
70	settling does not lock files, and deletion acts on source paths. Use trusted,
71	job-specific relay storage; do not fabricate acknowledgements or reuse old
72	protocol state for a different dataset. Neither deletion policy replaces backups.
73	
74	## Egress
75	
76	Backend subprocesses always have proxy environment variables stripped, including
77	when `egress = "any"`. The default `direct` policy rejects detected backend proxy
78	settings, fake-IP DNS in `198.18.0.0/15`, and routes through recognized tunnel
79	interfaces. Backend-internal proxy configuration and host routing still matter.
80	
81	Set `remote.egress = "any"`, or pass `--allow-proxy` to doctor/send/receive, only
82	when accepting those egress findings is intentional. This does not restore proxy
83	environment variables or fix missing authentication. `trusted_interfaces` exempts
84	interfaces you have independently verified route this backend directly. Host
85	checks cannot detect every transparent upstream proxy; verify cost-sensitive paths.
86	
87	## Unattended operation
88	
89	Preview a supervisor definition before installing anything:
90	
91	```sh
92	ferry service job.toml --side receiver
93	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
94	```
95	
96	Systemd user units run follow mode with `Restart=on-failure`; cron uses one-shot
97	commands and job locks prevent overlap. `--install` writes and enables the selected
98	service, so it can start transfers immediately; `--uninstall` removes it. Systemd
99	may need `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` to survive logout. On other supervisors,
100	including launchd, use the corresponding send/receive command explicitly. Test
101	manually with source retention before enabling any unattended destructive policy.
102
````

````text
1	# Configuration
2	
3	A job is a TOML file passed to each CLI command. Start with the complete
4	[local quickstart](getting-started.md), then change one setting at a time.
5	Use absolute filesystem paths for predictable behavior under supervisors.
6	
7	## Job identity and units
8	
9	`name` identifies the job; use letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens,
10	starting with a letter or digit. `state_dir` defaults to
11	`~/.local/state/ferry/<name>`. Keep it persistent and separate from source data.
12	Use a dedicated remote prefix for each job, not a shared production directory.
13	
14	`[units]` requires `root` and exactly one selection method:
15	
16	- `glob = "exports/*.parquet"`: each match is a unit, keyed from its basename.
17	  Avoid matches whose names collapse to the same key.
18	- `keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"` plus
19	  `members = ["data/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]`: derive each key from a file
20	  stem or directory name, then collect existing paths from the templates.
21	  Missing member paths are omitted; inspect `ferry plan` before sending.
22	
23	`pack = "tar"` is the default. `pack = "none"` requires exactly one regular file
24	per unit. Empty raw payloads are rejected; use tar when transporting empty files.
25	Keep unit paths non-overlapping, especially when extracting or deleting sources.
26	
27	| Optional unit setting | Behavior |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| `settle = "6h"` | Skip units whose newest file is younger than this; default is no delay. |
30	| `resend_changed = true` | Default; resend changed fingerprints when source deletion is `never`. |
31	| `recheck_recent = 30` | In follow mode, limit repeat checks to the last 30 sorted keys; unset checks all. |
32	
33	Fingerprints use relative paths and file sizes, **not content hashes**. Same-size
34	edits can go unnoticed. Restarting the sender performs a full fingerprint scan,
35	not a full content comparison. Settling is a heuristic, not a filesystem snapshot.
36	
37	## Sender and receiver
38	
39	| Section / setting | Purpose |
40	| --- | --- |
41	| `sender.stage_dir` | Local staging; defaults to `<state_dir>/stage`. |
42	| `sender.stage_cap = "50GB"` | Pause new packing when staged data reaches the cap; not a hard disk quota. |
43	| `sender.read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]` | Block starting new packing during these windows; uploads continue. |
44	| `sender.delete_source = "never"` | Default; retain sources. See [deletion policies](operations.md#source-deletion). |
45	| `receiver.dest` | Required for receiving; supports `{key}` and slices such as `{key[0:4]}`. |
46	| `receiver.extract = false` | Default; keep tar archives. Raw files are placed under their payload filenames. |
47	| `receiver.min_free = "20GB"` | Require this floor plus about twice the payload size before receiving. |
48	
49	With `extract = true`, tar member paths are extracted beneath `dest`; affected
50	unit paths are replaced wholesale. Use a dedicated destination, not directories
51	containing unrelated files. Leave room beyond the staging cap for a whole unit.
52	
53	## Relay and adapter selection
54	
55	`[remote]` requires `adapter` and `prefix`. Sizes accept strings such as `50GB`
56	or `3900MiB`. Optional `part_size` controls splitting; defaults depend on the
57	adapter. `min_free` is enforced only when the adapter can report free space.
58	`max_inflight` limits outstanding payload bytes tracked for the job; allow at
59	least the largest whole unit, or sending can wait indefinitely.
60	
61	| Adapter | Main `options` | Requirements and limits |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| `local` | `root` | Existing directory; no backend CLI. Both sides must see the same relay contents. |
64	| `baidupcs` | `binary`, `upload_threads`, `download_threads` | Authenticated BaiduPCS-Go; default parts are 3900 MiB, download threads 4. |
65	| `rclone` | `remote`, `flags`, `endpoints` | Configured rclone remote, e.g. `gdrive:`. Set endpoint hostnames if inference fails. |
66	| `ghrelease` | `repo`, `tag` | Authenticated `gh`; creates a missing draft release and refuses a published one. Default parts 1900 MiB, each strictly below 2 GiB. |
67	| `rsync` | `host`, `root`, `ssh_options`, `flags` | rsync and, for a remote host, working noninteractive SSH; empty `host` means local. |
68	
69	Ferry requires non-empty remote objects and uses its own SHA-256 verification,
70	not backend checksums. Backend quotas and permissions still apply.
71	
72	`[remote.sides.sender]` and `[remote.sides.receiver]` can override `adapter` and
73	`options`. An overridden options table **replaces**, rather than merges with,
74	the base options. For direct SSH delivery, send via rsync and receive locally:
75	
76	```toml
77	[remote]
78	adapter = "rsync"
79	prefix = "/inbox"
80	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
81	
82	[remote.sides.receiver]
83	adapter = "local"
84	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
85	```
86	
87	This is a fragment, not a complete job. The receiver runs on `nas` and reads the
88	same landing directory. `egress = "direct"` is the default; see
89	[egress controls](operations.md#egress) before accepting proxy routes.
90	
91	## Example jobs
92	
93	Adapt paths and review policies before using these public repository examples:
94	
95	- [Incremental mirror](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/mirror-incremental.toml): retains sources and extracts at the destination.
96	- [Baidu archive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/daily-archive-baidu.toml): **deletes sources after remote size checks**; change to `never` for a pilot.
97	- [Google Drive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/gdrive-via-proxy.toml): explicitly accepts non-direct egress.
98	- [GitHub draft release](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/github-draft-release.toml): raw-file units; replace the repository placeholder.
99
````

31

````text
1	# Getting started
2	
3	## Install
4	
5	With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed and Python 3.11+ available:
6	
7	```sh
8	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry
9	ferry --help
10	```
11	
12	Ensure uv's tool executable directory is on your `PATH`. The local adapter needs
13	no other tools or cloud account. Other adapters require their backend CLI and
14	separately configured authentication; never paste credential or session files
15	into a job, diagnostic report, or issue.
16	
17	## Try an isolated local relay
18	
19	Run these commands in one POSIX shell. They create a fresh temporary directory
20	containing a non-empty sample file, job state, staging, relay, and destination.
21	No existing dataset or cloud service is involved.
22	
23	```sh
24	demo=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ferry-demo.XXXXXX)
25	mkdir -p "$demo/source" "$demo/relay" "$demo/destination"
26	printf 'Hello from Ferry\n' > "$demo/source/hello.txt"
27	
28	cat > "$demo/job.toml" <<EOF
29	name = "local-demo"
30	state_dir = "$demo/state"
31	
32	[units]
33	root = "$demo/source"
34	glob = "*.txt"
35	pack = "none"
36	
37	[sender]
38	stage_dir = "$demo/stage"
39	delete_source = "never"
40	
41	[receiver]
42	dest = "$demo/destination"
43	extract = false
44	
45	[remote]
46	adapter = "local"
47	prefix = "/local-demo"
48	egress = "direct"
49	options = { root = "$demo/relay" }
50	EOF
51	
52	ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml"
53	ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
54	ferry plan "$demo/job.toml"
55	ferry send "$demo/job.toml"
56	ferry receive "$demo/job.toml" --once
57	ferry status "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
58	cmp "$demo/source/hello.txt" "$demo/destination/hello.txt"
59	printf 'Demo directory: %s\n' "$demo"
60	```
61	
62	Both doctor checks should report `OK`; plan and receiver status should each show

# Zensical site bootstrap

Build an English documentation site without adding application runtime
dependencies or publishing anything. This is a single-language pilot, separate
from `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`; existing MkDocs projects retain their old workflow.

Requires Python 3.11+ and `uv`. The tested builder is **Zensical 0.0.73**.

## When to use

- The user explicitly chooses Zensical for a new documentation site.
- A project is dogfooding Zensical before installing the published skill.
- A Zensical build succeeds but llms exports or Copy as Markdown are missing.
- The user wants to add pages or verify an existing Zensical site's artifacts.

## When not to use

- The user only asks for one Markdown document: do not scaffold a site.
- Existing MkDocs configuration, arbitrary plugins, hooks, or content-i18n
  requirements need migration analysis, not this initializer.
- English plus selected zh-TW, fallback, or contextual language switching is
  required now: prefer the existing MkDocs skill until that contract is tested.
- A generic request to "set up docs" is not permission to replace an existing
  engine. Inspect it and establish the desired scope first.

## Workflow

### 1. Confirm scope and inspect the project

Read project instructions, README, existing docs, `pyproject.toml`, task runner,
CI, `.gitignore`, and any recorded docs preferences. Keep the application's
runtime dependency contract. Do not reuse the MkDocs preference namespace or
change an explicit opt-out without the user's request.

Confirm an **English-only** initial site and which files are publishable. Do not
point `docs_dir` at the repository root or copy `backlog/`, agent history,
credentials, or runtime state into the site. A public repository is not consent
to enable Pages. Do not translate content automatically.

Read `references/pilot-and-migration.md` when comparing engines, planning later
translations, or replacing a local dogfood source with an installed skill.

### 2. Preview, then initialize

Use this skill's actual installed directory for the script path. Pass the
project root explicitly; never infer it from the agent's current directory.

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/init-docs-site.py" \
  --target-dir /path/to/project \
  --site-name 'My Project' \
  --repo-slug owner/project \
  --site-url https://owner.github.io/project/ \
  --ci --dry-run
```

After reviewing the plan and obtaining consent, repeat without `--dry-run`.
`--ci` adds a **build-only** workflow; omitting it creates no workflow.
For a reviewed nonempty `docs/`, add `--existing keep`. It requires an existing
`docs/index.md` and preserves the whole tree; it does not reorganize content.

The initializer refuses existing MkDocs/Zensical config, symlinks, and collisions
with generated paths. There is no `--force` mode. Re-running on a configured
project stops without changes: switch to maintenance instead.

### 3. Add development-only dependencies and build

Existing `pyproject.toml` is left untouched; follow the initializer's JSON
`next_steps` after reviewing the proposed dependency group:

```bash
uv add --group docs 'zensical==0.0.73'
uv sync --locked --only-group docs
uv run --no-sync zensical build --strict
uv run --no-sync python scripts/check-docs-site.py
```

A docs-only project without a prior `pyproject.toml` receives a non-packaged uv
project with Python >=3.11 and a docs group; run `uv lock` first instead of `uv add`.
Keep `uv.lock` under version control. Inspect its diff: do not silently upgrade
unrelated dependencies or replace an existing package index.

`--only-group docs` is suitable for CI. For local work that also needs the
application/dev dependencies, use `uv sync --locked --group docs` instead.
Do not put Zensical in `[project].dependencies` merely to make a build work.

The project-local checker verifies root and nested pages, full text, Markdown
counterparts, Copy as Markdown targets, project-subpath links, and a nonempty
search artifact. Fix failures instead of dropping strict mode. Its contract is
all `docs/**/*.md` pages; custom exclusions, output layouts, or plugins require
reviewing and adapting the checker as part of the same change.

### 4. Maintain project-owned documentation

Add English `.md` pages under `docs/` and keep relative links correct. The
initial config uses automatic navigation and llmstxt globs for root and nested
pages; no separate page helper is needed. If the user wants an explicit `nav`,
maintain it alongside the pages. Do not create locale-suffixed placeholders.

Preserve the README as a useful repository entrypoint. Link it to `docs/index.md`
until a site is actually published; a future `site_url` is not a live website.
Add commands to the project's existing Makefile/Justfile rather than replacing
its task runner. Run its normal checks as well as the documentation checks.

For preview:

```bash
uv run --no-sync zensical serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8000
# If that port is occupied, choose another without stopping the existing service:
uv run --no-sync zensical serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8769
```

Expose the address in the project's task runner instead of hard-coding port 8000.
For Just, use an optional port followed by an optional host:

```just
docs-serve port="8000" host="127.0.0.1":
    uv run --locked --group docs zensical serve --dev-addr "{{host}}:{{port}}"
```

`just docs-serve 8769` stays on loopback. A host such as `0.0.0.0` exposes the
preview to other machines; use it only when sharing is intentional.

The template enables Mermaid fences through `pymdownx.superfences.custom_fences`.
For process diagrams, keep node/edge labels explicit and supply a text equivalent.
Check rendered SVGs in light and dark mode; static build success does not prove
Mermaid syntax/layout or browser rendering.

In a browser, test navigation, search, and Copy as Markdown, including a nested
page. Check the clipboard content, not only that a button exists. Building the
site is not proof of interactive behavior.

### 5. Publish only after separate approval

The bundled workflow has no Pages permissions, deployment job, or public
preview. Do not enable Pages, dispatch deployment, or push changes merely
because initialization succeeded.

When explicitly asked to publish, read the current official
[Pages guide](https://zensical.org/docs/publish-your-site/). Adapt its artifact
flow to the existing locked docs group and checker. Keep PRs build-only; deploy
only approved default-branch events. Scope `pages: write` and `id-token: write`
to the deploy job, preserve project-subpath URLs, and confirm repo visibility.

## Available scripts

- `scripts/init-docs-site.py` — stdlib-only, no install/network/deploy operations.
  Flags: `--target-dir`, `--site-name`, `--site-url`, `--repo-slug`,
  `--existing keep`, `--ci`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  JSON stdout; diagnostics on stderr. Exit 0 success/preview, 2 blocked input.
- Project-local `scripts/check-docs-site.py` — copied from the asset below.
  Flags: `--target-dir` (defaults to CWD), `--help`. JSON stdout, diagnostics on
  stderr; exit 0 validated, 1 failed. It does not rebuild or publish anything.

## Bundled assets

- `assets/zensical.toml.template` — English theme, native copy/llmstxt, root and
  nested Markdown selection; no custom MkDocs plugin lifecycle.
- `assets/index.md.template` — starter page only for an empty docs tree.
- `assets/docs-check.yml` — locked build and artifact checks, no deployment.
- `assets/check-docs-site.py` — project-owned output-contract checker.

## Reference files

- `references/pilot-and-migration.md` — read before dogfooding, upgrading the
  builder, switching to a distributed skill, or considering multilingual docs.

## Gotchas

- **`**/*.md` alone can silently omit root pages.** The tested native llmstxt
  implementation needs `*.md` as well. Strict build can pass with empty exports.
- **Mermaid's rendered SVG lives in a closed shadow root in the tested release.**
  `pre.mermaid svg` / `.mermaid svg` selectors can time out even when the diagram
  is visible. Screenshot the `.mermaid` host and inspect its layout in both
  themes; host dimensions alone are not proof of correct rendering.
- **UI translation is not content i18n.** An alternate-language selector does
  not create translated pages or implement missing-translation fallback.
- **Zensical does not execute arbitrary MkDocs plugins.** Unsupported settings
  may be ignored; this pilot's checker allows only search and llmstxt plugins.
- **Upstream `zensical new` includes a deployment workflow with unpinned install.**
  Do not run it blindly inside a real project; this skill uses reviewed,
  build-only templates instead.
- **Installing/updating a skill does not migrate generated project files.**
  Keep the docs, config, checker and CI self-contained. Compare explicit changes
  after an update; never rerun initialization with an imagined force flag.
- **A local preview cannot prove GitHub Pages configuration.** Report local
  validation separately from installation, remote CI, and publication.

````text
145	## Commands
146	
147	```bash
148	ferry doctor job.toml [--side receiver]   # backend login, proxy settings, routes
149	ferry plan job.toml                       # units found under the source root
150	ferry send job.toml [--follow]            # until every unit is pushed (then marks done)
151	ferry receive job.toml [--once|--follow]  # until the sender is done and the relay is empty
152	ferry inventory job.toml [--root PATH]     # receiver: publish fingerprints for seeding
153	ferry status job.toml [--side receiver] [--scan-source] [--remote] [--json]
154	```
155	
156	A second sender (or receiver) for the same job on the same host exits immediately.
157	
158	### Running unattended
159	
160	ferry has no daemon of its own: `send`/`receive --follow` is a long-running loop that
161	polls for new or changed units. Put it under a supervisor; `ferry service` prints (or,
162	with `--install`, writes and enables) one:
163	
164	```bash
165	ferry service job.toml --side receiver                 # print a systemd user unit
166	ferry service job.toml --side receiver --install       # ~/.config/systemd/user/ferry-<job>-receiver.service
167	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
168	ferry service job.toml --side sender --uninstall
169	loginctl enable-linger $USER                           # let user services run without a login
170	```
171	
172	systemd units run `--follow` with `Restart=on-failure`; cron entries run one-shot
173	(`send`, `receive --once`) and rely on the job lock to skip overlapping runs. Any other
174	supervisor (pueue, tmux, launchd) works the same way: run the printed command.
175	
176	Library use (e.g. from an orchestrator):
177	
178	```python
179	import ferry
180	job = ferry.load_job("job.toml")
181	report = ferry.preflight(job, ferry.adapter_for(job, "sender"))
182	result = ferry.send(job)            # SendResult(pushed=..., pushed_bytes=..., ...)
183	st = ferry.side_status(job, "sender", remote=True)
184	```
185	
186	## Egress
187	
188	Proxy traffic is metered, so by default ferry insists on a direct path:
189	
190	1. `http(s)_proxy`, `all_proxy`, ... are removed from every backend process environment.
191	2. Backend tools' own proxy settings (BaiduPCS-Go `proxy`) are reported.
192	3. Each backend endpoint is resolved; a `198.18.0.0/15` answer (clash/mihomo fake-ip DNS)
193	   or a route via `tun*`/`utun*`/`Meta`/`wg*`/`tailscale*` is reported.
194	
195	With `egress = "direct"` any finding fails `send`/`receive`; `egress = "any"` (or
196	`--allow-proxy` for one run) accepts them with warnings — for backends that are only
197	reachable through a proxy, e.g. Google Drive from mainland China, where the proxy's own
198	rules may still pick DIRECT for some hosts. A transparent proxy on the router is not
199	visible from the host and cannot be detected.
200	
201	## Backend notes
202	
203	See [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — e.g. Baidu silently drops empty files and exits 0 on
204	errors, single-threaded Baidu downloads are ~4x slower, GitHub assets are limited to 2 GiB.
205
````

1	"""Subprocess execution for backend CLIs: proxy-free environment, quiet logs.
2	
3	Transfer tools print progress bars with carriage returns many times per second; those
4	lines are dropped from the log (only the final progress line of each run is kept) so a
5	multi-week transfer does not produce gigabytes of log.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import re
10	import subprocess
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from .egress import clean_env
14	
15	_PROGRESS = re.compile(r"[↑↓]|\d+(\.\d+)?%|Transferred:|ETA ")
16	
17	
18	class CommandError(RuntimeError):
19	    def __init__(self, argv: list[str], code: int, output: str):
20	        tail = "\n".join(output.strip().splitlines()[-5:])
21	        super().__init__(f"{argv[0]} {argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ''} exited {code}: {tail}")
22	        self.argv, self.code, self.output = argv, code, output
23	
24	
25	def run(argv: list[str], *, log: Path | None = None, timeout: float | None = None,
26	        check: bool = True) -> str:
27	    """Run quickly-returning commands and return combined stdout+stderr."""
28	    proc = subprocess.run(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True,
29	                          env=clean_env(), timeout=timeout, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
30	    if log is not None:
31	        _append(log, argv, proc.stdout)
32	    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
33	        raise CommandError(argv, proc.returncode, proc.stdout)
34	    return proc.stdout
35	
36	
37	def run_transfer(argv: list[str], *, log: Path | None = None) -> str:
38	    """Run a long transfer, streaming output; progress lines are not kept in the log."""
39	    kept: list[str] = []
40	    last_progress = ""
41	    with subprocess.Popen(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
42	                          env=clean_env(), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL) as proc:
43	        buf = b""
44	        assert proc.stdout is not None
45	        while chunk := proc.stdout.read1(65536):
46	            buf += chunk
47	            *lines, buf = re.split(rb"[\r\n]", buf)
48	            for raw in lines:
49	                line = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip()
50	                if not line:
51	                    continue
52	                if _PROGRESS.search(line):
53	                    last_progress = line
54	                else:
55	                    kept.append(line)
56	        if buf.strip():
57	            kept.append(buf.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
58	        code = proc.wait()
59	    if last_progress:
60	        kept.append(last_progress)
61	    output = "\n".join(kept)
62	    if log is not None:
63	        _append(log, argv, output)
64	    if code != 0:
65	        raise CommandError(argv, code, output)
66	    return output
67	
68	
69	def _append(log: Path, argv: list[str], output: str) -> None:
70	    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
71	    with log.open("a") as f:
72	        f.write("$ " + " ".join(argv) + "\n" + output.rstrip() + "\n")

55	    sources = sorted(docs.rglob("*.md"))

57	
58	    def local_file(url):
59	        parsed = urlsplit(url)
60	        require((parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc) == (origin.scheme, origin.netloc),
61	                f"artifact URL uses a different origin: {url}")
62	        require(parsed.path.startswith(origin.path), f"artifact URL drops the project subpath: {url}")

64	        path = (site / relative).resolve()
65	        require(path.is_relative_to(site.resolve()), f"artifact URL escapes site/: {url}")
66	        if parsed.path.endswith("/"):
67	            path /= "index.html"
68	        require(path.is_file(), f"missing artifact for {url}")

71	    index = (site / "llms.txt").read_text()
72	    full = (site / "llms-full.txt").read_text()
73	    links = re.findall(r"^\s*-\s+\[.*?\]\(<?([^)>\s]+)>?\)", index, re.MULTILINE)
74	    exported = [local_file(link) for link in links]
75	    require(len(exported) == len(set(exported)), "duplicate pages in llms.txt")
76	    expected = set()
77	    for source in sources:
78	        relative = source.relative_to(docs)
79	        directory = relative.parent if relative.name == "index.md" else relative.with_suffix("")
80	        markdown = site / directory / "index.md"
81	        html = site / directory / "index.html"
82	        expected.add(markdown.resolve())
83	        require(markdown.is_file() and html.is_file(), f"missing HTML/Markdown pair for {relative}")
84	        content = markdown.read_text().strip()
85	        require(content and content in full, f"full output omits content from {relative}")
86	        page = Page(html.read_text())
87	        html_url = urljoin(base, html.relative_to(site).as_posix())
88	        require(page.copy_urls, f"missing Copy as Markdown button for {relative}")
89	        for url in page.copy_urls:
90	            require(local_file(urljoin(html_url, url)) == markdown.resolve(),
91	                    f"copy button selects the wrong source for {relative}")
92	        for href in page.links:
93	            if href.startswith("#"):
94	                continue
95	            url = urljoin(html_url, href)
96	            parsed = urlsplit(url)
97	            if (parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc) == (origin.scheme, origin.netloc):
98	                local_file(url)
99	    require(set(exported) == expected, "llms.txt does not cover exactly the intended Markdown pages")
100	    search = json.loads((site / "search.json").read_text())
101	    require(isinstance(search, dict) and isinstance(search.get("items"), list)
102	            and bool(search["items"]), "empty or invalid search index: expected nonempty items")
103	    return {"status": "ok", "pages": len(sources), "llm_pages": len(exported), "deployed": False}

105	
106	def main():
107	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
108	    parser.add_argument("--target-dir", default=".", help="Project root containing zensical.toml")
109	    args = parser.parse_args()
110	    try:
111	        result = check(Path(args.target_dir).resolve())
112	    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
113	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
114	        print(json.dumps({"status": "failed", "deployed": False}))
115	        return 1
116	    print(json.dumps(result))
117	    return 0
118	
119	
120	if __name__ == "__main__":
121	    sys.exit(main())

````text
1	# Driving a remote pueued
2	
3	Pueue can't schedule *across* hosts (that's Slurm / K8s / Ray territory), but a
4	local `pueue` client **can** drive a `pueued` on another machine — and it gets
5	full control, not read-only status: `add`, `kill`, `log`, `follow` all work.
6	
7	Whether you should is a different question. Read "Just SSH over instead" first.
8	
9	> Everything below was verified against a real macOS client (pueue 4.0.4)
10	> driving a Linux `pueued` (4.0.2) over SSH unix-socket forwarding.
11	
12	## Just SSH over instead
13	
14	For most work, this is the correct answer and needs no setup at all:
15	
16	```bash
17	ssh myhost 'pueue add --label train-seed1 -- ./train.sh'
18	ssh myhost 'pueue status --json' | jq .
19	```
20	
21	The remote client runs on the remote box, so paths, environment, and logs are
22	all consistent. Nothing to configure, no secret to copy, no cert to sync.
23	
24	Reach for a real remote connection only when you want **local composition** —
25	a `pueue status --json` you can pipe straight into `jq` without an SSH round
26	trip per call, or a script/agent that shells out to `pueue` many times.
27	
28	Even then, the upstream wiki steers you away from exposing the daemon:
29	
30	> "If that's not safe enough for your use-case, you can always listen on
31	> unix-sockets/localhost and do port/unix-socket forwarding via SSH."
32	
33	So the recommended setup is **SSH forwarding**, below. Direct TCP exposure is
34	the last resort, not the default.
35	
36	## Recommended: SSH unix-socket forwarding
37	
38	The daemon keeps its default unix socket and **needs no reconfiguration** —
39	you change nothing on the server. Only the client gets a config.
40	
41	### 1. Find the daemon's socket
42	
43	```bash
44	ssh myhost 'ls /run/user/$(id -u)/pueue_*.socket'
45	# /run/user/1000/pueue_myuser.socket
46	```
47	
48	`unix_socket_path: null` in the server's config means this default location.
49	
50	### 2. Copy the shared secret
51	
52	The client authenticates with the *same* secret file as the daemon:
53	
54	```bash
55	mkdir -p ~/.config/pueue/remote && chmod 700 ~/.config/pueue/remote
56	ssh myhost 'cat ~/.local/share/pueue/shared_secret' > ~/.config/pueue/remote/shared_secret
57	chmod 600 ~/.config/pueue/remote/shared_secret
58	```
59	
60	### 3. Write a client-only config
61	
62	Keep it separate from your local config and select it with `-c`:
63	
64	```yaml
65	# ~/.config/pueue/remote/client.yml
66	client:
67	  read_local_logs: false          # REQUIRED — see Gotchas
68	shared:
69	  use_unix_socket: true
70	  unix_socket_path: /home/you/.config/pueue/remote/remote.sock
71	  shared_secret_path: /home/you/.config/pueue/remote/shared_secret
72	```
73	
74	### 4. Forward the socket, then talk to it
75	
76	```bash
77	ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
78	    -L ~/.config/pueue/remote/remote.sock:/run/user/1000/pueue_myuser.socket \
79	    myhost
80	
81	pueue -c ~/.config/pueue/remote/client.yml status
82	```
83	
84	Add `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3` for a long-lived
85	tunnel, or manage it with `autossh` / a systemd user unit. Remove the stale
86	local socket file before re-forwarding.
87	
88	Because the tunnel terminates at the daemon's own unix socket, **no TLS
89	certificate is involved** — the `daemon_cert` / TCP plumbing below only applies
90	if you skip SSH.
91	
92	## Alternative: direct TCP + TLS
93	
94	Only if SSH forwarding genuinely doesn't fit. Requires editing the server's
95	config and **restarting `pueued`**, which interrupts a running queue.
96	
97	On the daemon: `use_unix_socket: false`, plus a reachable `host` and `port`.
98	Pueue self-signs a TLS certificate at startup; the client verifies against a
99	copy of it:
100	
101	| Client key | Points at |
102	|---|---|
103	| `shared_secret_path` | copy of the daemon's `shared_secret` |
104	| `daemon_cert` | copy of the daemon's `daemon.cert` |
105	| `host` / `port` | the daemon's listen address |
106	| `use_unix_socket: false` | required |
107	
108	The client "will only connect to a pueued daemon which serves the known
109	certificate", so the cert must be re-copied whenever the daemon regenerates it.
110	
111	## Gotchas
112	
113	- **`read_local_logs: false` is mandatory on a remote client.** Left at the
114	  default `true`, the client tries to read task logs off its *own* disk, where
115	  the remote daemon's log directory does not exist. Set it false and logs come
116	  back over the connection instead. `log` and `follow` were verified working
117	  this way.
118	
119	- **The working directory is resolved on the CLIENT, and this is the thing
120	  that will bite you.** Pueue records a task's cwd at submit time and
121	  canonicalizes it locally. Three distinct failures, all observed:
122	
123	  | You do | What happens |
124	  |---|---|
125	  | `pueue add -- ./x.sh` from a local dir | Local cwd is sent. On the daemon it doesn't exist → task ends `FailedToSpawn`, never runs. |
126	  | `--working-directory /home/you` (remote-only path) | Client **refuses to submit**: `Failed to canonicalize given working directory path`. |
127	  | `--working-directory /tmp` from macOS | Silently rewritten to `/private/tmp` (macOS symlink) → `FailedToSpawn` on Linux. |
128	
129	  Only a path that exists **and canonicalizes identically on both machines**
130	  works — verified with `--working-directory /usr`, which ran correctly and
131	  returned the remote hostname.
132	
133	  This makes cross-platform remote submission (macOS client → Linux daemon)
134	  impractical for real jobs, since your project paths won't exist locally.
135	  **`ssh myhost 'pueue add ...'` has none of this problem** and is the right
136	  tool for submitting. A forwarded client is still excellent for *reading*
137	  (`status --json`, `log`) and for `kill` / `pause` / `restart`.
138	
139	- **A `FailedToSpawn` task is `Done`, not `Failed`.** Its result is
140	  dict-shaped — `{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error>"}` — not the bare string the
````

Wait until tasks are finished.

By default, this will wait for all tasks in the default group to finish.

Note: This will also wait for all tasks that aren't somehow 'Done'. Includes: [Paused, Stashed,
Locked, Queued, ...]

Usage: pueue wait [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          This allows you to wait for specific tasks to finish

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Wait for all tasks in a specific group

  -a, --all
          Wait for all tasks across all groups and the default group

  -q, --quiet
          Don't show any log output while waiting

  -s, --status <STATUS>
          Wait for tasks to reach a specific task status

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
Set the amount of allowed parallel tasks

By default, adjusts the amount of the default group.

No tasks will be stopped, if this is lowered. This limit is only considered when tasks are
scheduled.

Usage: pueue parallel [OPTIONS] [PARALLEL_TASKS]

Arguments:
  [PARALLEL_TASKS]
          The amount of allowed parallel tasks.
          
          Setting this to 0 means an unlimited amount of parallel tasks.

Options:
  -g, --group <group>
          Set the amount for a specific group

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups.

Kills all tasks of the default group when no ids or a specific group are provided.

Usage: pueue kill [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          Kill these specific tasks

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Kill all running tasks in a group. This also pauses the group

  -a, --all
          Kill all running tasks across ALL groups. This also pauses all groups

  -s, --signal <SIGNAL>
          Send a UNIX signal instead of simply killing the process.
          
          DISCLAIMER: This bypasses Pueue's process handling logic! You might enter weird invalid
          states, use at your own descretion.
          
          This argument also excepts the integer representation as well as the signal short name.
          E.g. `sigint`, `int`, or `2` are the same.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

## Queueing 必須說清楚的行為

| 行為 | 已確認的注意事項 |
|---|---|
| `send`，不加 follow | 一輪候選掃描、推送完才寫 done marker；**不代表有時間上限**。可等待讀取時窗、staging／remote 容量、in-flight 限制與 ACK。 |
| 上傳重試 | `_push_unit()` 例外持續重試，backoff 30 秒倍增至 600 秒，沒有次數上限；queue task 可能一直 Running，而非 Failed。 |
| `receive` | 預設等「sender done 且 relay 無 unit 目錄」；`--follow` 不因完成而退出。 |
| `receive --once` | 只掃描一輪；尚未有 manifest 或目的地空間不足的單位可能沒接收，仍成功退出。不是「完整接收一批」保證。 |
| 接收重試 | 單位失敗保留並續跑；一般／follow 模式會再嘗試，沒有次數上限；無進展時依 poll 等待。 |
| 鎖定 | `<state_dir>/<side>.lock` 的非阻塞 `flock`；同 state／side 第二實例退出 **2**，不是成功跳過，也不是跨主機分散式鎖。sender 與 receiver 可並行。 |
| 中止／exit code | 明確處理的設定／preflight／lock 錯誤為 2、回傳結果含 failed 為 1、KeyboardInterrupt 為 130。SIGTERM 只設 stop event，可能未完成卻回傳 0；backend transfer runner 沒有 stop-event 傳播或 transfer timeout。 |

**兩個重要跨檔結論：**

- `delete_source="after_receiver_ack"` 要 receiver 同時工作；remote backpressure 也可能需要 receiver 消耗 relay。因此把 receiver 排在 sender 成功之後，或兩者放在只有一個 slot 的 group，可能互相等待。

## pueue 文件建議

現況：README 只有一句「pueue、tmux、launchd 也可」，正式 operations 頁沒有 pueue 範例。

- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/ferry/README.md:158–174`
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/ferry/docs/operations.md:87–101`

建議新增：

- **有限批次**：示範 dedicated group、每個 job／side 序列化、明確 label、絕對 job 路徑及 backend PATH／登入前置要求。
- **串行範例限定條件**：只對小型、relay 放得下、沒有等待 receiver ACK／清空 relay 的批次，示範成功後執行 `receive --once`。
- **有 ACK／容量背壓**：receiver 必須獨立並行；跨主機在各自主機提交，不把本地 pueue 當分散式排程器。
- **持續同步**：優先現有 systemd／其他 service supervisor；不要把 `--follow` 放進預期會完成的 dependency chain。
- **狀態與重試**：pueue 的程序成功不等於全部資料完成；同時查看 Ferry ledger/status。重試保留 state、stage、partial，勿清空續傳狀態。
- **週期排程**：由 cron／timer 觸發，不把 pueue 當內建週期 scheduler。

另外，`doctor` **不是無副作用的設定驗證器**：文件明示 rsync doctor 可能建立 landing directory；`plan` 只列單位，不模擬 settling／刪除／傳輸。

98	def _duration(value: str | int | float) -> float:
99	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
100	        return float(value)
101	    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([smhd]?)\s*", value)
102	    if not m:
103	        raise JobError(f"invalid duration {value!r}; use e.g. '30m', '6h', '2d'")
104	    return float(m.group(1)) * {"": 1, "s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600, "d": 86400}[m.group(2)]
105	
106	
107	def _path(value: str) -> Path:
108	    return Path(os.path.expandvars(os.path.expanduser(value)))

126	                          settle_seconds=_duration(u.get("settle", 0)),

130	            raise JobError("units needs exactly one of keys_from (+members) or glob")
131	        if units.keys_from and not units.members:

140	            delete_source=s.get("delete_source", "never"))
141	        if sender.delete_source not in DELETE_POLICIES:
142	            raise JobError(f"sender.delete_source must be one of {DELETE_POLICIES}")
143	        receiver = None
144	        if "receiver" in data:
145	            rc = data["receiver"]
146	            receiver = ReceiverSpec(dest=rc["dest"], extract=bool(rc.get("extract", False)),
147	                                    min_free=parse_size(rc.get("min_free", 0)) or 0)
148	        remote = RemoteSpec(adapter=r["adapter"], prefix=r["prefix"].rstrip("/"),
149	                            part_size=parse_size(r.get("part_size")),
150	                            min_free=parse_size(r.get("min_free", 0)) or 0,
151	                            max_inflight=parse_size(r.get("max_inflight")),
152	                            egress=r.get("egress", "direct"),
153	                            trusted_interfaces=tuple(r.get("trusted_interfaces", ())),
154	                            options=dict(r.get("options", {})),
155	                            sides=dict(r.get("sides", {})))
156	        if set(remote.sides) - {"sender", "receiver"}:
157	            raise JobError("remote.sides keys must be 'sender' or 'receiver'")
158	        if remote.egress not in EGRESS_POLICIES:
159	            raise JobError(f"remote.egress must be one of {EGRESS_POLICIES}")
160	    except KeyError as e:

162	    return Job(name, path, state_dir, units, sender, receiver, remote)

165	def enumerate_units(spec: UnitsSpec) -> list[Unit]:
166	    """All units currently present under the source root, sorted by key."""
167	    root = spec.root
168	    units: dict[str, Unit] = {}
169	    if spec.keys_from:
170	        for match in root.glob(spec.keys_from):
171	            key = match.stem if match.is_file() else match.name
172	            if not _KEY.fullmatch(key):
173	                raise JobError(f"derived key {key!r} is not a safe name")
174	            members = tuple(m for m in (t.format(key=key) for t in spec.members)
175	                            if (root / m).exists())
176	            units[key] = Unit(key, root, members)
177	    else:
178	        for match in root.glob(spec.glob or ""):
179	            # Remote names starting with "_" are reserved for protocol files.
180	            key = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", match.name).lstrip("._-")
181	            if key in units:
182	                raise JobError(f"two glob matches map to key {key!r}")
183	            units[key] = Unit(key, root, (str(match.relative_to(root)),))
184	    if spec.pack == "none":
185	        for unit in units.values():
186	            if len(unit.members) != 1 or not (root / unit.members[0]).is_file():
187	                raise JobError(f"pack='none' needs exactly one regular file per unit ({unit.key})")
188	    return [units[k] for k in sorted(units)]
189	
190	
191	def dest_dir(receiver: ReceiverSpec, key: str) -> Path:
192	    def slice_(m: re.Match) -> str:
193	        a, b = (int(x) if x else None for x in (m.group(1), m.group(2)))
194	        return key[a:b]
195	
196	    text = re.sub(r"\{key\[(-?\d*):(-?\d*)\]\}", slice_, receiver.dest).replace("{key}", key)
197	    return _path(text)

1	"""Generate (and optionally install) a supervisor entry for a job side.
2	
3	Two kinds:
4	
5	* ``systemd`` (default on Linux): a *user* service running ``ferry send|receive --follow``
6	  with ``Restart=on-failure``. Survives logout/reboot only with lingering enabled
7	  (``loginctl enable-linger $USER``); ``ferry service`` reports the current state.
8	* ``cron``: a one-shot run on a schedule (``send`` without ``--follow``, ``receive
9	  --once``). Overlapping runs are harmless: the per-job lock makes the second exit.
10	
11	Without ``--install`` the unit / crontab line is only printed, so it can be reviewed or
12	managed by other tooling (ansible, chezmoi, ...).
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import getpass
17	import shlex
18	import shutil
19	import subprocess
20	import sys
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	from .job import Job
24	
25	UNIT_DIR = Path("~/.config/systemd/user").expanduser()
26	CRON_TAG = "# ferry:"
27	
28	
29	def _ferry_argv() -> list[str]:
30	    exe = shutil.which("ferry")
31	    return [exe] if exe else [sys.executable, "-m", "ferry.cli"]
32	
33	
34	def command(job: Job, side: str, *, follow: bool, poll: float | None) -> list[str]:
35	    if job.path is None:
36	        raise ValueError("job must be loaded from a file to build a service")
37	    verb = "send" if side == "sender" else "receive"
38	    argv = [*_ferry_argv(), verb, str(job.path.resolve())]
39	    if follow:
40	        argv.append("--follow")
41	    elif side == "receiver":
42	        argv.append("--once")
43	    if poll is not None:
44	        argv += ["--poll", f"{poll:g}"]
45	    return argv
46	
47	
48	def unit_name(job: Job, side: str) -> str:
49	    return f"ferry-{job.name}-{side}.service"
50	
51	
52	def systemd_unit(job: Job, side: str, *, poll: float | None) -> str:
53	    argv = command(job, side, follow=True, poll=poll)
54	    return f"""[Unit]
55	Description=ferry {side} for job {job.name}
56	After=network-online.target
57	Wants=network-online.target
58	
59	[Service]
60	Type=simple
61	ExecStart={shlex.join(argv)}
62	Restart=on-failure
63	RestartSec=60
64	# ferry strips proxy variables for backend tools itself; keep the unit environment minimal.
65	Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
66	
67	[Install]
68	WantedBy=default.target
69	"""
70	
71	
72	def cron_line(job: Job, side: str, schedule: str, *, poll: float | None) -> str:
73	    argv = command(job, side, follow=False, poll=poll)
74	    return f"{schedule} {shlex.join(argv)} >/dev/null 2>&1 {CRON_TAG}{job.name}:{side}"
75	
76	
77	def linger_enabled() -> bool | None:
78	    try:
79	        out = subprocess.run(["loginctl", "show-user", getpass.getuser(), "-p", "Linger"],
80	                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout
81	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
82	        return None
83	    return out.strip().endswith("=yes") if out.strip() else None
84	
85	
86	def _systemctl(*args: str) -> None:
87	    subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", *args], check=True)
88	
89	
90	def install_systemd(job: Job, side: str, *, poll: float | None) -> Path:
91	    UNIT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
92	    path = UNIT_DIR / unit_name(job, side)
93	    path.write_text(systemd_unit(job, side, poll=poll))
94	    _systemctl("daemon-reload")
95	    _systemctl("enable", "--now", path.name)
96	    return path
97	
98	
99	def uninstall_systemd(job: Job, side: str) -> None:
100	    path = UNIT_DIR / unit_name(job, side)
101	    subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "disable", "--now", path.name], check=False)
102	    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
103	    _systemctl("daemon-reload")
104	
105	
106	def _crontab() -> list[str]:
107	    out = subprocess.run(["crontab", "-l"], capture_output=True, text=True)
108	    return out.stdout.splitlines() if out.returncode == 0 else []
109	
110	
111	def _write_crontab(lines: list[str]) -> None:
112	    subprocess.run(["crontab", "-"], input="\n".join(lines) + "\n", text=True, check=True)
113	
114	
115	def install_cron(job: Job, side: str, schedule: str, *, poll: float | None) -> str:
116	    tag = f"{CRON_TAG}{job.name}:{side}"
117	    line = cron_line(job, side, schedule, poll=poll)
118	    _write_crontab([x for x in _crontab() if not x.endswith(tag)] + [line])
119	    return line
120	
121	
122	def uninstall_cron(job: Job, side: str) -> None:
123	    tag = f"{CRON_TAG}{job.name}:{side}"
124	    _write_crontab([x for x in _crontab() if not x.endswith(tag)])

````text
1	# Operations
2	
3	## Inspect before transferring
4	
5	```sh
6	ferry doctor job.toml
7	ferry doctor job.toml --side receiver
8	ferry plan job.toml
9	ferry status job.toml
10	ferry status job.toml --side receiver --json
11	ferry status job.toml --scan-source --remote
12	```
13	
14	Doctor checks the selected backend and egress; it can contact remote services
15	and, for rsync, create a missing landing directory. It is not a generic dry-run
16	or proof that every later backend operation will succeed. Plan enumerates source
17	units and members; it does not simulate transfer, settling, or source deletion.
18	
19	Status normally reads local ledgers. `--scan-source` adds source enumeration;
20	`--remote` queries the backend for relay information. Sender and receiver have
21	separate state, so inspect each on its own host. Commands accept `--json`, but
22	service output remains supervisor text rather than a general JSON report.
23	
24	## Run and resume
25	
26	```sh
27	ferry send job.toml
28	ferry receive job.toml --once
29	```
30	
31	Send processes eligible work and marks the sender done. Receive with `--once`
32	makes one pass; without it, receive waits until the sender is done and the relay
33	is empty. For continuous operation, run `send --follow` and `receive --follow`
34	in separate processes, adding `--poll 60` to control idle polling in seconds.
35	
36	To resume, restart the same command with the same job, state, staging, and relay
37	prefix. Do not delete ledgers, staged manifests, or destination partial files to
38	"fix" an interrupted transfer. Uploaded parts with matching remote sizes can be
39	reused; downloaded parts are checked by SHA-256 before reuse. One sender and one
40	receiver may run per job on a host; a second instance of either side fails fast.
41	
42	Inspect `<state_dir>/sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`, and side logs when progress
43	stalls. Check read windows, settling, staging space, remote limits, destination
44	free space, and preflight errors. Keep credentials and session files out of reports.
45	
46	## Integrity and destination safety
47	
48	The sender hashes the packed payload and its parts. The receiver checks sizes,
49	part and whole-payload SHA-256 hashes, and tar member counts before recording
50	verification. It then removes that unit's relay data. With extraction enabled,
51	existing unit paths are replaced, including removal of files absent in the new copy.
52	
53	Change detection is weaker than transfer verification: its path-and-size
54	fingerprints miss same-size edits. `ferry inventory job.toml --no-upload --json`
55	previews fingerprints of an existing destination tree; omit `--no-upload` only
56	when you intend to publish them to the relay for sender-side skipping. Use
57	`--root PATH` for a source-shaped tree when `receiver.dest` contains a key template.
58	Inventory seeding is not a content-hash audit or evidence of a fresh transfer.
59	
60	## Source deletion
61	
62	- `never` is the default and the recommended starting point.
63	- `after_remote_size` deletes source members after upload size checks, **before
64	  destination SHA-256 verification**. Use only for independently recoverable data.
65	- `after_receiver_ack` waits for the receiver's verification acknowledgement.
66	  Keep the sender running or restart it to consume acknowledgements; one-shot
67	  sending can wait for the receiver rather than exiting immediately.
68	
69	Keep source units immutable throughout transfer and acknowledgement handling:
70	settling does not lock files, and deletion acts on source paths. Use trusted,
71	job-specific relay storage; do not fabricate acknowledgements or reuse old
72	protocol state for a different dataset. Neither deletion policy replaces backups.
73	
74	## Egress
75	
76	Backend subprocesses always have proxy environment variables stripped, including
77	when `egress = "any"`. The default `direct` policy rejects detected backend proxy
78	settings, fake-IP DNS in `198.18.0.0/15`, and routes through recognized tunnel
79	interfaces. Backend-internal proxy configuration and host routing still matter.
80	
81	Set `remote.egress = "any"`, or pass `--allow-proxy` to doctor/send/receive, only
82	when accepting those egress findings is intentional. This does not restore proxy
83	environment variables or fix missing authentication. `trusted_interfaces` exempts
84	interfaces you have independently verified route this backend directly. Host
85	checks cannot detect every transparent upstream proxy; verify cost-sensitive paths.
86	
87	## Unattended operation
88	
89	Preview a supervisor definition before installing anything:
90	
91	```sh
92	ferry service job.toml --side receiver
93	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
94	```
95	
96	Systemd user units run follow mode with `Restart=on-failure`; cron uses one-shot
97	commands and job locks prevent overlap. `--install` writes and enables the selected
98	service, so it can start transfers immediately; `--uninstall` removes it. Systemd
99	may need `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` to survive logout. On other supervisors,
100	including launchd, use the corresponding send/receive command explicitly. Test
101	manually with source retention before enabling any unattended destructive policy.
102
````
