````text
1	# Configuration
2	
3	A job is a TOML file passed to each CLI command. Start with the complete
4	[local quickstart](getting-started.md), then change one setting at a time.
5	Use absolute filesystem paths for predictable behavior under supervisors.
6	
7	## Job identity and units
8	
9	`name` identifies the job; use letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens,
10	starting with a letter or digit. `state_dir` defaults to
11	`~/.local/state/ferry/<name>`. Keep it persistent and separate from source data.
12	Use a dedicated remote prefix for each job, not a shared production directory.
13	
14	`[units]` requires `root` and exactly one selection method:
15	
16	- `glob = "exports/*.parquet"`: each match is a unit, keyed from its basename.
17	  Avoid matches whose names collapse to the same key.
18	- `keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"` plus
19	  `members = ["data/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]`: derive each key from a file
20	  stem or directory name, then collect existing paths from the templates.
21	  Missing member paths are omitted; inspect `ferry plan` before sending.
22	
23	`pack = "tar"` is the default. `pack = "none"` requires exactly one regular file
24	per unit. Empty raw payloads are rejected; use tar when transporting empty files.
25	Keep unit paths non-overlapping, especially when extracting or deleting sources.
26	
27	| Optional unit setting | Behavior |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| `settle = "6h"` | Skip units whose newest file is younger than this; default is no delay. |
30	| `resend_changed = true` | Default; resend changed fingerprints when source deletion is `never`. |
31	| `recheck_recent = 30` | In follow mode, limit repeat checks to the last 30 sorted keys; unset checks all. |
32	
33	Fingerprints use relative paths and file sizes, **not content hashes**. Same-size
34	edits can go unnoticed. Restarting the sender performs a full fingerprint scan,
35	not a full content comparison. Settling is a heuristic, not a filesystem snapshot.
36	
37	## Sender and receiver
38	
39	| Section / setting | Purpose |
40	| --- | --- |
41	| `sender.stage_dir` | Local staging; defaults to `<state_dir>/stage`. |
42	| `sender.stage_cap = "50GB"` | Pause new packing when staged data reaches the cap; not a hard disk quota. |
43	| `sender.read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]` | Block starting new packing during these windows; uploads continue. |
44	| `sender.delete_source = "never"` | Default; retain sources. See [deletion policies](operations.md#source-deletion). |
45	| `receiver.dest` | Required for receiving; supports `{key}` and slices such as `{key[0:4]}`. |
46	| `receiver.extract = false` | Default; keep tar archives. Raw files are placed under their payload filenames. |
47	| `receiver.min_free = "20GB"` | Require this floor plus about twice the payload size before receiving. |
48	
49	With `extract = true`, tar member paths are extracted beneath `dest`; affected
50	unit paths are replaced wholesale. Use a dedicated destination, not directories
51	containing unrelated files. Leave room beyond the staging cap for a whole unit.
52	
53	## Relay and adapter selection
54	
55	`[remote]` requires `adapter` and `prefix`. Sizes accept strings such as `50GB`
56	or `3900MiB`. Optional `part_size` controls splitting; defaults depend on the
57	adapter. `min_free` is enforced only when the adapter can report free space.
58	`max_inflight` limits outstanding payload bytes tracked for the job; allow at
59	least the largest whole unit, or sending can wait indefinitely.
60	
61	| Adapter | Main `options` | Requirements and limits |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| `local` | `root` | Existing directory; no backend CLI. Both sides must see the same relay contents. |
64	| `baidupcs` | `binary`, `upload_threads`, `download_threads` | Authenticated BaiduPCS-Go; default parts are 3900 MiB, download threads 4. |
65	| `rclone` | `remote`, `flags`, `endpoints` | Configured rclone remote, e.g. `gdrive:`. Set endpoint hostnames if inference fails. |
66	| `ghrelease` | `repo`, `tag` | Authenticated `gh`; creates a missing draft release and refuses a published one. Default parts 1900 MiB, each strictly below 2 GiB. |
67	| `rsync` | `host`, `root`, `ssh_options`, `flags` | rsync and, for a remote host, working noninteractive SSH; empty `host` means local. |
68	
69	Ferry requires non-empty remote objects and uses its own SHA-256 verification,
70	not backend checksums. Backend quotas and permissions still apply.
71	
72	`[remote.sides.sender]` and `[remote.sides.receiver]` can override `adapter` and
73	`options`. An overridden options table **replaces**, rather than merges with,
74	the base options. For direct SSH delivery, send via rsync and receive locally:
75	
76	```toml
77	[remote]
78	adapter = "rsync"
79	prefix = "/inbox"
80	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
81	
82	[remote.sides.receiver]
83	adapter = "local"
84	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
85	```
86	
87	This is a fragment, not a complete job. The receiver runs on `nas` and reads the
88	same landing directory. `egress = "direct"` is the default; see
89	[egress controls](operations.md#egress) before accepting proxy routes.
90	
91	## Example jobs
92	
93	Adapt paths and review policies before using these public repository examples:
94	
95	- [Incremental mirror](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/mirror-incremental.toml): retains sources and extracts at the destination.
96	- [Baidu archive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/daily-archive-baidu.toml): **deletes sources after remote size checks**; change to `never` for a pilot.
97	- [Google Drive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/gdrive-via-proxy.toml): explicitly accepts non-direct egress.
98	- [GitHub draft release](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/github-draft-release.toml): raw-file units; replace the repository placeholder.
99
````

1	"""Subprocess execution for backend CLIs: proxy-free environment, quiet logs.
2	
3	Transfer tools print progress bars with carriage returns many times per second; those
4	lines are dropped from the log (only the final progress line of each run is kept) so a
5	multi-week transfer does not produce gigabytes of log.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import re
10	import subprocess
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from .egress import clean_env
14	
15	_PROGRESS = re.compile(r"[↑↓]|\d+(\.\d+)?%|Transferred:|ETA ")
16	
17	
18	class CommandError(RuntimeError):
19	    def __init__(self, argv: list[str], code: int, output: str):
20	        tail = "\n".join(output.strip().splitlines()[-5:])
21	        super().__init__(f"{argv[0]} {argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else ''} exited {code}: {tail}")
22	        self.argv, self.code, self.output = argv, code, output
23	
24	
25	def run(argv: list[str], *, log: Path | None = None, timeout: float | None = None,
26	        check: bool = True) -> str:
27	    """Run quickly-returning commands and return combined stdout+stderr."""
28	    proc = subprocess.run(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True,
29	                          env=clean_env(), timeout=timeout, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
30	    if log is not None:
31	        _append(log, argv, proc.stdout)
32	    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
33	        raise CommandError(argv, proc.returncode, proc.stdout)
34	    return proc.stdout
35	
36	
37	def run_transfer(argv: list[str], *, log: Path | None = None) -> str:
38	    """Run a long transfer, streaming output; progress lines are not kept in the log."""
39	    kept: list[str] = []
40	    last_progress = ""
41	    with subprocess.Popen(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
42	                          env=clean_env(), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL) as proc:
43	        buf = b""
44	        assert proc.stdout is not None
45	        while chunk := proc.stdout.read1(65536):
46	            buf += chunk
47	            *lines, buf = re.split(rb"[\r\n]", buf)
48	            for raw in lines:
49	                line = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip()
50	                if not line:
51	                    continue
52	                if _PROGRESS.search(line):
53	                    last_progress = line
54	                else:
55	                    kept.append(line)
56	        if buf.strip():
57	            kept.append(buf.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
58	        code = proc.wait()
59	    if last_progress:
60	        kept.append(last_progress)
61	    output = "\n".join(kept)
62	    if log is not None:
63	        _append(log, argv, output)
64	    if code != 0:
65	        raise CommandError(argv, code, output)
66	    return output
67	
68	
69	def _append(log: Path, argv: list[str], output: str) -> None:
70	    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
71	    with log.open("a") as f:
72	        f.write("$ " + " ".join(argv) + "\n" + output.rstrip() + "\n")
73

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/ferry/.claude/skills/pueue-job-queue

# pueue job queue

Pueue is a daemon-backed shell job queue. The daemon (`pueued`) accepts tasks
via the `pueue` CLI, runs them across parallelism-capped **groups**, persists
state across reboots, and exposes status / logs as JSON. This skill teaches
the agent to drive pueue end-to-end: submit single tasks or whole DAGs, cap
parallelism per group, block until completion, retrieve logs, and retry.

The skill is a **CLI bridge**, not a scheduler. Pueue's `--after` is **AND-only**
and **success-only** — that maps cleanly to declarative DAGs and not much
beyond. For OR-deps, conditional branching, retry-with-backoff, or distributed
scheduling, escalate to a real orchestrator (see "When NOT to use").

## When to use

- "Run these 30 commands, max 4 at a time" → `pueue group add ml && pueue parallel 4 --group ml` then loop `submit.sh --group ml`.
- "Kick off a long training job and let me close my laptop" → `submit.sh -- ./train.sh` (pueue persists across reboots).
- "Run task B only after task A finishes successfully" → `submit.sh --after $A_ID -- ./b.sh`.
- "Fan out 4 trainings, then evaluate" → `submit-dag.py dag.yaml`.
- "Schedule this for tonight" → `submit.sh --delay 6h -- ./nightly.sh`.
- "Block until task 17 is done, then tell me what happened" → `wait.py --ids 17`.
- The user mentions pueue, pueued, the pueue CLI, or asks about a "task queue for shell jobs".

## When NOT to use

- **One short shell command** the user wants to run right now. Just run it. Pueue adds daemon overhead for nothing.
- **Cross-host *scheduling*** (jobs distributed across N machines) → Airflow / Dagster / Prefect / Slurm. Note this is not the same as driving a *single* remote daemon, which pueue does support — see `references/remote-daemon.md`.
- **Conditional / OR / retry-with-backoff dependencies** → real orchestrator. Pueue's `--after` is AND-only and success-only.
- **Typed task IO and artifact tracking** (data lineage, cached intermediate outputs) → DVC (`dvc exp run --queue`), Prefect, Airflow.
- **Long-running services** (web servers, daemons) → systemd, launchd, supervisord. Pueue is for finite tasks.

## Authoritative sources

- Repo: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue
- Wiki: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki
- `pueue --help`, `pueue <subcommand> --help`, `man pueue`

## Mental model

| Concept | What it is | How to interact |
|---|---|---|
| **Daemon** (`pueued`) | Long-running process holding queue state. Required. | `pueued -d` to start. `pueue shutdown` to stop. |
| **Task** | One shell command, identified by integer id. | `pueue add ...`, `pueue status`, `pueue kill`, `pueue remove`. |
| **Group** | Named queue with its own parallelism limit. `default` always exists. | `pueue group add <name>`, `pueue parallel N --group <name>`. |
| **Dependency** | Task waits for one or more parents to **succeed** before running. | `pueue add --after <id> --after <id> -- <cmd>`. AND-only, success-only. |
| **Status** | Tagged enum: `Queued`, `Running`, `Stashed`, `Paused`, `Locked`, `Done`. `Done` carries a `result` (`Success`, `Killed`, `DependencyFailed`, or `{"Failed": <exit_code>}`). | `pueue status --json`. |

## Setup quickstart

```bash
# 1. Verify daemon is healthy. Auto-start if missing.
bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/check-daemon.sh --start --json | jq

# 2. (Optional) Create a group with 4 parallel slots.
pueue group add ml
pueue parallel 4 --group ml
```

For per-OS daemon paths and launchd/systemd setup, read
`references/daemon-and-config.md`.

## Always pass a label

`pueue status` shows the **label** column before the command. In a busy
queue, scanning labels is the only way to tell `train.py` runs apart at a
glance. **Always pass `--label`** when submitting, and bias toward names
that distinguish *this* task from its siblings.

Convention:

- Shape: `<verb>-<subject>-<key>` (≤30 chars). `verb` = action,
  `subject` = artifact, `key` = the variable that distinguishes this run.
- Encode the discriminator: seed, dataset slice, model variant, date, host.
- Don't restate the command — `train.py --seed 1` becomes label
  `train-baseline-seed1`, not `python-train-py-seed-1`.
- For DAGs, `submit-dag.py --label-prefix <run>-` makes every task labeled
  `<run>-<task_name>` so `wait.py --label-prefix <run>-` selects the whole
  graph and `pueue clean` can be filtered later.

| Good | Bad |
|---|---|
| `train-baseline-seed1` | `task1` (no metadata) |
| `eval-prod-2026q1` | `python eval.py --quarter 2026q1` (restates cmd) |
| `fetch-prices-AAPL` | `fetch-data` (multiple identical labels) |
| `nightly-featurize` (DAG) | `step-2-of-5` (rename a step → label rots) |

## Workflow A — submit one task

```bash
bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
  --label train-baseline --group ml \
  -- python train.py --seed 1
# stdout: {"task_id":17,"label":"train-baseline","group":"ml","after":[],...}
# stderr: submitted task 17 (group=ml, label=train-baseline)
```

Capture the id with `jq -r .task_id`. The script wraps `pueue add
--print-task-id` and falls back to a status-by-label lookup if the id parse
fails (defensive against future format changes).

## Workflow B — batched runs with capped parallelism

```bash
# One-time: create + size the group
pueue group add sweep
pueue parallel 4 --group sweep

# Loop: submit 30 tasks; pueue runs at most 4 at a time
for SEED in $(seq 1 30); do
  bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
    --label "sweep-$SEED" --group sweep \
    -- python train.py --seed "$SEED"
done

# Block until all sweep-* tasks are done
skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py \
  --label-prefix sweep- --group sweep
```

Group parallelism is the parallelism primitive in pueue — there is no
per-task pool. Set it once, submit freely.

## Workflow C — fan-out / fan-in DAG

For multi-task pipelines with success-only dependencies, write a YAML spec
and submit it declaratively. **Prefer `--isolated-group`** — it creates a
fresh group sized to the DAG's fan-out width and leaves your other groups
(especially `default`) untouched:

```bash
skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit-dag.py \
  skills/local/pueue-job-queue/assets/dag.example.yaml \
  --label-prefix nightly- --isolated-group
# stderr: isolated-group: created 'dag-dcda9347' with parallel_tasks=2
# stdout: {"tasks":{"fetch":17,...},
#          "topo_order":[...],
#          "width_per_group":{"dag-dcda9347":2},
#          "isolated_group":"dag-dcda9347"}
```

Each task gets the label `<--label-prefix><task_name>` so you can
`wait.py --label-prefix nightly-` later. After the run, clean up with
`pueue group remove <name>` (or run `cleanup.sh --remove-empty-groups`).

The submitter topo-sorts, validates the graph (cycle detection, unknown
references, missing `cmd:`), computes the **DAG width per group** (the
minimum `parallel_tasks` needed for fan-out to actually run in parallel),
then submits in order — wiring `--after` from the in-flight name→id map.
**No partial submits**: validation fails loud before any `pueue add` runs.

Three parallelism modes, in order of recommendation:

1. **`--isolated-group [NAME]`** (recommended). Fresh group, sized to width,
   no side effects on other groups. NAME auto-generates from spec hash if
   omitted. Mutually exclusive with `--default-group`.
2. **`--auto-parallel`**. Mutates `pueue parallel` on the target group in
   place. Use this when the DAG is meant to live in a long-lived shared
   group (e.g. `ml`) and that group's parallelism should permanently grow.
3. **No flag**. Only warns (in stderr + JSON's `parallelism_warnings`).
   Useful in `--dry-run` planning.

See `assets/dag.example.yaml` for a 5-task fan-out/fan-in template and
`references/dag-patterns.md` for more shapes.

## Workflow D — block until tasks reach terminal state

```bash
# Wait for specific ids
skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --ids 17,18,19 --timeout-seconds 300

# Wait for everything in a group
skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --group ml

# Wait for a label prefix (e.g. all tasks the DAG submitter created)
skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --label-prefix nightly-
```

Output is a JSON summary on stdout:

```json
{"summary": {"total": 4, "success": 3, "failed": 1, "killed": 0, "dependency_failed": 0},
 "tasks": [{"id": 17, "status": "Done", "result": "Success", "exit_code": 0,
            "label": "nightly-fetch", "group": "ml",
            "start": "...", "end": "..."}],
 "elapsed_seconds": 42.3}
```

Exit codes: `0` all succeeded, `5` ≥1 task failed/killed/dependency-failed,
`6` timeout. The agent can branch on exit code instead of parsing JSON.

## Workflow E — logs, retry, kill

One-line `pueue` calls (full list in `references/cli-cheatsheet.md`):

```bash
pueue log --json --full 17        # full stdout/stderr as JSON
pueue restart --in-place 17       # retry in-place (overwrites old log)
pueue kill 17 && pueue remove 17  # kill + drop from queue
```

For ad-hoc filtering, prefer pueue's built-in QUERY DSL over piping
through `jq` — it's faster (server-side filter) and shorter:

```bash
pueue status --json 'status=Failed order_by end desc first 10'
pueue status --json 'label %= sweep-'   # substring match
```

See `references/json-schema.md` for the QUERY grammar + jq fallbacks.

## Workflow F — periodic cleanup

Pueue's task list grows unbounded. `pueue status --json` walks the whole
table, so a queue with thousands of completed tasks slows down everything
that touches status. Run `cleanup.sh` weekly:

```bash
skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/cleanup.sh \
  --successful-only --remove-empty-groups --logs-older-than 30
# stdout: {"cleaned_tasks":[...], "removed_groups":["dag-abc12345"],
#          "deleted_logs":[...], "kept_running":[...], ...}
```

`--successful-only` keeps failures around for inspection; drop the flag
for a full sweep. Pair with the agent's existing weekly maintenance habit
(or `/schedule` an agent to run it).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/check-daemon.sh`** — Single-shot daemon health + version + log-dir check, with optional auto-start. Outputs JSON to stdout.
  - Flags: `--start`, `--json` (default on), `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` healthy, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable, `4` client/daemon version mismatch.
- **`scripts/submit.sh`** — Submit ONE task, return clean JSON `{task_id, group, label, after, ...}`. Wraps `pueue add --print-task-id` with defensive id parsing. Auto-creates the group if missing.
  - Flags: `--label`, `--group`, `--after` (repeatable), `--immediate`, `--stashed`, `--delay`, `--priority`, `--working-dir`, `--escape`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` `pueue add` failed, `4` daemon unreachable.
- **`scripts/wait.py`** — Block until selected tasks reach terminal status; emit a JSON summary. Selectors: `--ids`, `--label`, `--label-prefix`, `--group`. Quiet by default — emits only one initial line + state-change events on stderr; pass `--verbose` for per-tick output.
  - Flags: `--ids`, `--label` (repeatable), `--label-prefix`, `--group`, `--poll-seconds`, `--timeout-seconds`, `--fail-fast`, `--verbose`, `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` all succeeded, `1` arg error, `4` daemon unreachable, `5` ≥1 failed/killed/dependency-failed, `6` timeout.
- **`scripts/submit-dag.py`** — Declarative DAG submitter. Reads YAML or JSON (file path or `-` for stdin), topo-sorts, validates, submits with wired `--after`, returns `{name → id, topo_order, width_per_group, isolated_group?}`. Computes DAG fan-out width per group; with `--isolated-group [NAME]` creates a fresh dedicated group sized to the width (preferred — leaves user's other groups untouched). With `--auto-parallel` mutates target groups in place. Without either, only warns.
  - Flags: `--format`, `--default-group`, `--label-prefix`, `--dry-run`, `--print-graph`, `--auto-parallel`, `--isolated-group [NAME]`, `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` all submitted, `1` schema/cycle/unknown-ref/conflicting flags, `2` pueue not installed, `3` mid-run pueue failure (stdout still emits IDs that DID submit, for cleanup).
- **`scripts/cleanup.sh`** — Prune pueue task history, empty groups, and old log files. Wraps `pueue clean` + `pueue group remove` for empty non-default groups + optional log-file mtime pruning. Emits a JSON report. Run weekly to keep `pueue status --json` fast.
  - Flags: `--successful-only`, `--group GROUP`, `--remove-empty-groups`, `--logs-older-than N`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` ok (or dry-run), `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable.

## Bundled assets

- `assets/dag.example.yaml` — 5-task fan-out/fan-in (`fetch → featurize → {train_a, train_b} → evaluate`). Pass it to `submit-dag.py` with `--dry-run` first to see the topo order.
- `assets/pueue.yml.example` — Config snippet showing `pause_group_on_failure: true`, `default_parallel_tasks`, and a sample `groups:` block. The header comment names the platform-specific destination paths.

## Reference files

- `references/cli-cheatsheet.md` — Read **when** the task needs `pueue follow`, `pueue log`, `pueue restart`, `pueue kill`, `pueue clean`, `pueue group/parallel`, `pueue pause/start`, `pueue reset`, `pueue edit`, `pueue env`, or any other un-wrapped `pueue` subcommand. Has a one-line "when to use" for each.
- `references/json-schema.md` — Read **when** writing custom `jq` queries against `pueue status --json` or `pueue log --json`, or when a script's JSON parsing surprises you. Documents the observed schema on pueue 4.0.2 with concrete examples for each status variant.
- `references/dag-patterns.md` — Read **when** the user asks for shapes beyond fan-out/fan-in (mixed sequential+parallel, diamond, etc.) or hits the AND-only / success-only limitation. Has examples and a "when to escalate to a real orchestrator" decision table.
- `references/daemon-and-config.md` — Read **when** setting up `pueued` for the first time, configuring per-OS paths, picking config knobs (`pause_group_on_failure`, `default_parallel_tasks`), or wiring up launchd / systemd-user.
- `references/remote-daemon.md` — Read **when** the daemon is on another machine: SSH unix-socket forwarding (recommended, needs no server change), direct TCP + TLS, and the working-directory trap that makes cross-platform remote *submission* impractical. Short version: `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client to read/control.

## See also

- `long-running-jobs` — pueue is one *implementation* of "let the queue own the
  chain" (`--after`) and "block once" (`wait.py`). That skill owns the prior
  question: **which** of those an agent should reach for, when a scheduled
  check-in is ever justified, and how to record completion durably so a run
  survives losing the session. Read it if you are tempted to poll
  `pueue status` on a timer.
- `slurm-hpc` — the cluster-side equivalent when jobs leave this machine.

## Gotchas

- **DAG fan-out is gated by `parallel_tasks` per group.** Even when two siblings both depend only on `A` and the DAG allows them to run in parallel, they will *serialize* if their group's `parallel_tasks=1`. Pueue's parallelism primitive is the group, not the dependency graph. `submit-dag.py` warns when DAG width exceeds the group's slots and suggests the exact `pueue parallel N --group G` command; pass `--auto-parallel` to apply it.
- **`pueue add -- bash -c 'sleep 60'` does not preserve quoting.** Pueue joins all `<COMMAND>` args and re-shells. The single-quoted `'sleep 60'` is unwrapped by *your* shell before pueue sees it, then pueue re-splits. Quote the **whole** command as one arg: `pueue add 'sleep 60'` or `submit.sh -- 'bash -c "sleep 60 && echo done"'`.
- **`--after` is AND-only and success-only.** Failed parent → dependent's `status.Done.result` becomes `"DependencyFailed"` and it never runs. There is no OR, no run-on-failure, no retry-on-failure. If you need that, you need a real orchestrator.
- **Pueue does NOT auto-create groups.** `pueue add --group new_name` exits 1 with `"Group new_name doesn't exists. Use one of these: [...]"`. `submit.sh` calls `pueue group add` first if the group is missing.
- **`pueue restart` (default) creates a NEW task id.** The old id stays in history with its result. To retry in-place (reusing the id, overwriting the log), pass `--in-place`. Choose deliberately — agent users often want `--in-place` for "retry this".
- **`pause_group_on_failure` is config-only, no CLI flag.** Set it in `pueue.yml`; reload with `pueue reset` or restart `pueued`.
- **Logs live in platform-specific dirs**, not your CWD. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/logs/`. Linux: `~/.local/share/pueue/logs/`. Windows: `%APPDATA%\pueue\logs\`. `pueue log --json --full <id>` reads them for you.
- **`pueue wait` returns 0 even if the waited-on tasks failed.** It blocks until terminal, period. To know success/failure, query `pueue status --json` afterward (or use `wait.py`, which does this for you and returns a non-zero exit on failures).
- **`pueue remove` requires each id as a separate positional arg** (not a space-joined string from a subshell). Use bash arrays: `IDS=($(...)) && pueue remove "${IDS[@]}"`.
- **`pueue clean --successful-only` is a flag, not the default.** Plain `pueue clean` removes ALL finished tasks (including failures, which you may want to keep for debugging). Be deliberate.
- **`pueue add --print-task-id` writes the bare integer to stdout.** No JSON, no prose. `submit.sh` parses with a regex that tolerates future format changes; if you bypass `submit.sh`, capture with `ID=$(pueue add --print-task-id ... )` directly.
- **A terminal result that isn't `Success` is a failure — don't enumerate the bad ones.** `result` is a tagged enum, and `{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error>"}` is dict-shaped, not the bare string older notes implied. Matching a known-bad list let it fall through as success, so `wait.py` returned `0` for a task that never started. It now allowlists `Success` and fails closed on anything else.
- **Driving a remote daemon: the working directory is resolved on the CLIENT.** `pueue add` records and canonicalizes the cwd locally, so submitting to a remote daemon fails three different ways — local cwd sent (task ends `FailedToSpawn`), remote-only path rejected outright (`Failed to canonicalize given working directory path`), or a macOS symlink silently rewritten (`/tmp` → `/private/tmp`). Use `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client is for reading and control. See `references/remote-daemon.md`.

# Zensical site bootstrap

Build an English documentation site without adding application runtime
dependencies or publishing anything. This is a single-language pilot, separate
from `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`; existing MkDocs projects retain their old workflow.

Requires Python 3.11+ and `uv`. The tested builder is **Zensical 0.0.73**.

## When to use

- The user explicitly chooses Zensical for a new documentation site.
- A project is dogfooding Zensical before installing the published skill.
- A Zensical build succeeds but llms exports or Copy as Markdown are missing.
- The user wants to add pages or verify an existing Zensical site's artifacts.

## When not to use

- The user only asks for one Markdown document: do not scaffold a site.
- Existing MkDocs configuration, arbitrary plugins, hooks, or content-i18n
  requirements need migration analysis, not this initializer.
- English plus selected zh-TW, fallback, or contextual language switching is
  required now: prefer the existing MkDocs skill until that contract is tested.
- A generic request to "set up docs" is not permission to replace an existing
  engine. Inspect it and establish the desired scope first.

## Workflow

### 1. Confirm scope and inspect the project

Read project instructions, README, existing docs, `pyproject.toml`, task runner,
CI, `.gitignore`, and any recorded docs preferences. Keep the application's
runtime dependency contract. Do not reuse the MkDocs preference namespace or
change an explicit opt-out without the user's request.

Confirm an **English-only** initial site and which files are publishable. Do not
point `docs_dir` at the repository root or copy `backlog/`, agent history,
credentials, or runtime state into the site. A public repository is not consent
to enable Pages. Do not translate content automatically.

Read `references/pilot-and-migration.md` when comparing engines, planning later
translations, or replacing a local dogfood source with an installed skill.

### 2. Preview, then initialize

Use this skill's actual installed directory for the script path. Pass the
project root explicitly; never infer it from the agent's current directory.

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/init-docs-site.py" \
  --target-dir /path/to/project \
  --site-name 'My Project' \
  --repo-slug owner/project \
  --site-url https://owner.github.io/project/ \
  --ci --dry-run
```

After reviewing the plan and obtaining consent, repeat without `--dry-run`.
`--ci` adds a **build-only** workflow; omitting it creates no workflow.
For a reviewed nonempty `docs/`, add `--existing keep`. It requires an existing
`docs/index.md` and preserves the whole tree; it does not reorganize content.

The initializer refuses existing MkDocs/Zensical config, symlinks, and collisions
with generated paths. There is no `--force` mode. Re-running on a configured
project stops without changes: switch to maintenance instead.

### 3. Add development-only dependencies and build

Existing `pyproject.toml` is left untouched; follow the initializer's JSON
`next_steps` after reviewing the proposed dependency group:

```bash
uv add --group docs 'zensical==0.0.73'
uv sync --locked --only-group docs
uv run --no-sync zensical build --strict
uv run --no-sync python scripts/check-docs-site.py
```

A docs-only project without a prior `pyproject.toml` receives a non-packaged uv
project with Python >=3.11 and a docs group; run `uv lock` first instead of `uv add`.
Keep `uv.lock` under version control. Inspect its diff: do not silently upgrade
unrelated dependencies or replace an existing package index.

`--only-group docs` is suitable for CI. For local work that also needs the
application/dev dependencies, use `uv sync --locked --group docs` instead.
Do not put Zensical in `[project].dependencies` merely to make a build work.

The project-local checker verifies root and nested pages, full text, Markdown
counterparts, Copy as Markdown targets, project-subpath links, and a nonempty
search artifact. Fix failures instead of dropping strict mode. Its contract is
all `docs/**/*.md` pages; custom exclusions, output layouts, or plugins require
reviewing and adapting the checker as part of the same change.

### 4. Maintain project-owned documentation

Add English `.md` pages under `docs/` and keep relative links correct. The
initial config uses automatic navigation and llmstxt globs for root and nested
pages; no separate page helper is needed. If the user wants an explicit `nav`,
maintain it alongside the pages. Do not create locale-suffixed placeholders.

Preserve the README as a useful repository entrypoint. Link it to `docs/index.md`
until a site is actually published; a future `site_url` is not a live website.
Add commands to the project's existing Makefile/Justfile rather than replacing
its task runner. Run its normal checks as well as the documentation checks.

For preview:

```bash
uv run --no-sync zensical serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8000
# If that port is occupied, choose another without stopping the existing service:
uv run --no-sync zensical serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8769
```

Expose the address in the project's task runner instead of hard-coding port 8000.
For Just, use an optional port followed by an optional host:

```just
docs-serve port="8000" host="127.0.0.1":
    uv run --locked --group docs zensical serve --dev-addr "{{host}}:{{port}}"
```

`just docs-serve 8769` stays on loopback. A host such as `0.0.0.0` exposes the
preview to other machines; use it only when sharing is intentional.

The template enables Mermaid fences through `pymdownx.superfences.custom_fences`.
For process diagrams, keep node/edge labels explicit and supply a text equivalent.
Check rendered SVGs in light and dark mode; static build success does not prove
Mermaid syntax/layout or browser rendering.

In a browser, test navigation, search, and Copy as Markdown, including a nested
page. Check the clipboard content, not only that a button exists. Building the
site is not proof of interactive behavior.

### 5. Publish only after separate approval

The bundled workflow has no Pages permissions, deployment job, or public
preview. Do not enable Pages, dispatch deployment, or push changes merely
because initialization succeeded.

When explicitly asked to publish, read the current official
[Pages guide](https://zensical.org/docs/publish-your-site/). Adapt its artifact
flow to the existing locked docs group and checker. Keep PRs build-only; deploy
only approved default-branch events. Scope `pages: write` and `id-token: write`
to the deploy job, preserve project-subpath URLs, and confirm repo visibility.

## Available scripts

- `scripts/init-docs-site.py` — stdlib-only, no install/network/deploy operations.
  Flags: `--target-dir`, `--site-name`, `--site-url`, `--repo-slug`,
  `--existing keep`, `--ci`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  JSON stdout; diagnostics on stderr. Exit 0 success/preview, 2 blocked input.
- Project-local `scripts/check-docs-site.py` — copied from the asset below.
  Flags: `--target-dir` (defaults to CWD), `--help`. JSON stdout, diagnostics on
  stderr; exit 0 validated, 1 failed. It does not rebuild or publish anything.

## Bundled assets

- `assets/zensical.toml.template` — English theme, native copy/llmstxt, root and
  nested Markdown selection; no custom MkDocs plugin lifecycle.
- `assets/index.md.template` — starter page only for an empty docs tree.
- `assets/docs-check.yml` — locked build and artifact checks, no deployment.
- `assets/check-docs-site.py` — project-owned output-contract checker.

## Reference files

- `references/pilot-and-migration.md` — read before dogfooding, upgrading the
  builder, switching to a distributed skill, or considering multilingual docs.

## Gotchas

- **`**/*.md` alone can silently omit root pages.** The tested native llmstxt
  implementation needs `*.md` as well. Strict build can pass with empty exports.
- **Mermaid's rendered SVG lives in a closed shadow root in the tested release.**
  `pre.mermaid svg` / `.mermaid svg` selectors can time out even when the diagram
  is visible. Screenshot the `.mermaid` host and inspect its layout in both
  themes; host dimensions alone are not proof of correct rendering.
- **UI translation is not content i18n.** An alternate-language selector does
  not create translated pages or implement missing-translation fallback.
- **Zensical does not execute arbitrary MkDocs plugins.** Unsupported settings
  may be ignored; this pilot's checker allows only search and llmstxt plugins.
- **Upstream `zensical new` includes a deployment workflow with unpinned install.**
  Do not run it blindly inside a real project; this skill uses reviewed,
  build-only templates instead.
- **Installing/updating a skill does not migrate generated project files.**
  Keep the docs, config, checker and CI self-contained. Compare explicit changes
  after an update; never rerun initialization with an imagined force flag.
- **A local preview cannot prove GitHub Pages configuration.** Report local
  validation separately from installation, remote CI, and publication.

1	"""Generate (and optionally install) a supervisor entry for a job side.

3	Two kinds:
4	
5	* ``systemd`` (default on Linux): a *user* service running ``ferry send|receive --follow``
6	  with ``Restart=on-failure``. Survives logout/reboot only with lingering enabled
7	  (``loginctl enable-linger $USER``); ``ferry service`` reports the current state.
8	* ``cron``: a one-shot run on a schedule (``send`` without ``--follow``, ``receive
9	  --once``). Overlapping runs are harmless: the per-job lock makes the second exit.
10	
11	Without ``--install`` the unit / crontab line is only printed, so it can be reviewed or
12	managed by other tooling (ansible, chezmoi, ...).
13	"""

23	from .job import Job

34	def command(job: Job, side: str, *, follow: bool, poll: float | None) -> list[str]:
35	    if job.path is None:
36	        raise ValueError("job must be loaded from a file to build a service")
37	    verb = "send" if side == "sender" else "receive"
38	    argv = [*_ferry_argv(), verb, str(job.path.resolve())]
39	    if follow:
40	        argv.append("--follow")
41	    elif side == "receiver":
42	        argv.append("--once")
43	    if poll is not None:
44	        argv += ["--poll", f"{poll:g}"]
45	    return argv
46	
47	
48	def unit_name(job: Job, side: str) -> str:
49	    return f"ferry-{job.name}-{side}.service"
50	
51	
52	def systemd_unit(job: Job, side: str, *, poll: float | None) -> str:
53	    argv = command(job, side, follow=True, poll=poll)
54	    return f"""[Unit]
55	Description=ferry {side} for job {job.name}
56	After=network-online.target
57	Wants=network-online.target
58	
59	[Service]
60	Type=simple
61	ExecStart={shlex.join(argv)}
62	Restart=on-failure
63	RestartSec=60
64	# ferry strips proxy variables for backend tools itself; keep the unit environment minimal.
65	Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

67	[Install]
68	WantedBy=default.target

93	    path.write_text(systemd_unit(job, side, poll=poll))

100	    path = UNIT_DIR / unit_name(job, side)
101	    subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "disable", "--now", path.name], check=False)

108	    return out.stdout.splitlines() if out.returncode == 0 else []
109	
110	
111	def _write_crontab(lines: list[str]) -> None:
112	    subprocess.run(["crontab", "-"], input="\n".join(lines) + "\n", text=True, check=True)
113	
114	
115	def install_cron(job: Job, side: str, schedule: str, *, poll: float | None) -> str:
116	    tag = f"{CRON_TAG}{job.name}:{side}"
117	    line = cron_line(job, side, schedule, poll=poll)
118	    _write_crontab([x for x in _crontab() if not x.endswith(tag)] + [line])
119	    return line

121	
122	def uninstall_cron(job: Job, side: str) -> None:
123	    tag = f"{CRON_TAG}{job.name}:{side}"
124	    _write_crontab([x for x in _crontab() if not x.endswith(tag)])

165	def enumerate_units(spec: UnitsSpec) -> list[Unit]:
166	    """All units currently present under the source root, sorted by key."""
167	    root = spec.root
168	    units: dict[str, Unit] = {}
169	    if spec.keys_from:
170	        for match in root.glob(spec.keys_from):
171	            key = match.stem if match.is_file() else match.name
172	            if not _KEY.fullmatch(key):
173	                raise JobError(f"derived key {key!r} is not a safe name")
174	            members = tuple(m for m in (t.format(key=key) for t in spec.members)
175	                            if (root / m).exists())
176	            units[key] = Unit(key, root, members)
177	    else:
178	        for match in root.glob(spec.glob or ""):
179	            # Remote names starting with "_" are reserved for protocol files.
180	            key = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", match.name).lstrip("._-")
181	            if key in units:
182	                raise JobError(f"two glob matches map to key {key!r}")
183	            units[key] = Unit(key, root, (str(match.relative_to(root)),))
184	    if spec.pack == "none":
185	        for unit in units.values():
186	            if len(unit.members) != 1 or not (root / unit.members[0]).is_file():
187	                raise JobError(f"pack='none' needs exactly one regular file per unit ({unit.key})")

78	@contextmanager
79	def instance_lock(job: Job, side: str):
80	    """One sender and one receiver per job and host; a second instance fails fast."""
81	    job.state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
82	    path = job.state_dir / f"{side}.lock"
83	    fh = path.open("a+")
84	    try:
85	        fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
86	    except BlockingIOError:
87	        fh.seek(0)
88	        holder = fh.read().strip() or "?"
89	        fh.close()
90	        raise AlreadyRunning(f"another ferry {side} for job {job.name} is running "
91	                             f"(pid {holder}, lock {path})") from None
92	    fh.seek(0)
93	    fh.truncate()
94	    fh.write(str(os.getpid()))
95	    fh.flush()
96	    try:
97	        yield
98	    finally:
99	        fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
100	        fh.close()

1	# Getting started
2	
3	## Install
4	
5	With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed and Python 3.11+ available:
6	
7	```sh
8	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry
9	ferry --help
10	```
11	
12	Ensure uv's tool executable directory is on your `PATH`. The local adapter needs
13	no other tools or cloud account. Other adapters require their backend CLI and
14	separately configured authentication; never paste credential or session files
15	into a job, diagnostic report, or issue.
16	
17	## Try an isolated local relay
18	
19	Run these commands in one POSIX shell. They create a fresh temporary directory
20	containing a non-empty sample file, job state, staging, relay, and destination.
21	No existing dataset or cloud service is involved.
22	
23	```sh
24	demo=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ferry-demo.XXXXXX)
25	mkdir -p "$demo/source" "$demo/relay" "$demo/destination"
26	printf 'Hello from Ferry\n' > "$demo/source/hello.txt"
27	
28	cat > "$demo/job.toml" <<EOF
29	name = "local-demo"
30	state_dir = "$demo/state"
31	
32	[units]
33	root = "$demo/source"
34	glob = "*.txt"
35	pack = "none"
36	
37	[sender]
38	stage_dir = "$demo/stage"
39	delete_source = "never"
40	
41	[receiver]
42	dest = "$demo/destination"
43	extract = false
44	
45	[remote]
46	adapter = "local"
47	prefix = "/local-demo"
48	egress = "direct"
49	options = { root = "$demo/relay" }
50	EOF
51	
52	ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml"
53	ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
54	ferry plan "$demo/job.toml"
55	ferry send "$demo/job.toml"
56	ferry receive "$demo/job.toml" --once
57	ferry status "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
58	cmp "$demo/source/hello.txt" "$demo/destination/hello.txt"
59	printf 'Demo directory: %s\n' "$demo"
60	```
61	
62	Both doctor checks should report `OK`; plan and receiver status should each show
63	one unit. `cmp` exits successfully without output when files match. The source
64	remains intact; verified relay payloads are removed, but protocol files may remain.
65	Keep the printed directory to inspect or repeat the job: using the same state
66	resumes recorded work rather than forcing a fresh copy. The demo directory remains.
67	
68	## Move to two hosts
69	
70	Use matching job names, unit definitions, and relay prefixes, with host-appropriate
71	paths and persistent state on each host. Start with a small disposable dataset and
72	`delete_source = "never"`; run doctor for each side before sending.
73	Choose a backend in [Configuration](configuration.md), then read
74	[Operations](operations.md) before enabling follow mode or source deletion.
75
````

1	# ferry — agent instructions
2	
3	Standalone, stdlib-only Python (>=3.11) tool. Keep it dependency-free: target hosts are
4	often old (CentOS 7 via uv-managed Python), without root, with restricted egress.
5	
6	- Checks: `just check` (ruff + pytest). Tests that touch real clouds are marked
7	  `network` and skipped by default (`uv run pytest -m network`).
8	- Every backend command must go through `ferry.proc.run`/`run_transfer` so proxy
9	  variables are stripped (`egress.clean_env`). Never call `subprocess` directly.
10	- Never trust backend checksums; verify with our own sha256 and sizes.
11	- Every remote object must be non-empty (Baidu drops empty files).
12	- Never read, print or log backend credentials/session files.
13	- Ledger formats (`sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`) and the manifest are compatibility
14	  surfaces: bump `MANIFEST_VERSION` and handle old records when changing them.
15	- Record backend traps in `pitfalls/` (titled by symptom); future work in `TODO.md`.
16	- Do not commit or push without an explicit request.
17	- Documentation uses an English Zensical pilot: `just docs-setup`, `just docs-build`,
18	  `just docs-serve`. Keep Zensical in the `docs` dependency group, never runtime deps.
19	  Preserve `docs/` and `zensical.toml`; do not apply the MkDocs recipe from installed
20	  generic Python skills. The workflow checks pull requests and publishes GitHub
21	  Pages from `main`; Pages publishing was explicitly authorized by the user.
22	  No multilingual fallback is implemented in this pilot.
23
```
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Configuration
2	
3	A job is a TOML file passed to each CLI command. Start with the complete
4	[local quickstart](getting-started.md), then change one setting at a time.
5	Use absolute filesystem paths for predictable behavior under supervisors.
6	
7	## Job identity and units
8	
9	`name` identifies the job; use letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens,
10	starting with a letter or digit. `state_dir` defaults to
11	`~/.local/state/ferry/<name>`. Keep it persistent and separate from source data.
12	Use a dedicated remote prefix for each job, not a shared production directory.
13	
14	`[units]` requires `root` and exactly one selection method:
15	
16	- `glob = "exports/*.parquet"`: each match is a unit, keyed from its basename.
17	  Avoid matches whose names collapse to the same key.
18	- `keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"` plus
19	  `members = ["data/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]`: derive each key from a file
20	  stem or directory name, then collect existing paths from the templates.
21	  Missing member paths are omitted; inspect `ferry plan` before sending.
22	
23	`pack = "tar"` is the default. `pack = "none"` requires exactly one regular file
24	per unit. Empty raw payloads are rejected; use tar when transporting empty files.
25	Keep unit paths non-overlapping, especially when extracting or deleting sources.
26	
27	| Optional unit setting | Behavior |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| `settle = "6h"` | Skip units whose newest file is younger than this; default is no delay. |
30	| `resend_changed = true` | Default; resend changed fingerprints when source deletion is `never`. |
31	| `recheck_recent = 30` | In follow mode, limit repeat checks to the last 30 sorted keys; unset checks all. |
32	
33	Fingerprints use relative paths and file sizes, **not content hashes**. Same-size
34	edits can go unnoticed. Restarting the sender performs a full fingerprint scan,
35	not a full content comparison. Settling is a heuristic, not a filesystem snapshot.
36	
37	## Sender and receiver
38	
39	| Section / setting | Purpose |
40	| --- | --- |
41	| `sender.stage_dir` | Local staging; defaults to `<state_dir>/stage`. |
42	| `sender.stage_cap = "50GB"` | Pause new packing when staged data reaches the cap; not a hard disk quota. |
43	| `sender.read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]` | Block starting new packing during these windows; uploads continue. |
44	| `sender.delete_source = "never"` | Default; retain sources. See [deletion policies](operations.md#source-deletion). |
45	| `receiver.dest` | Required for receiving; supports `{key}` and slices such as `{key[0:4]}`. |
46	| `receiver.extract = false` | Default; keep tar archives. Raw files are placed under their payload filenames. |
47	| `receiver.min_free = "20GB"` | Require this floor plus about twice the payload size before receiving. |
48	
49	With `extract = true`, tar member paths are extracted beneath `dest`; affected
50	unit paths are replaced wholesale. Use a dedicated destination, not directories
51	containing unrelated files. Leave room beyond the staging cap for a whole unit.
52	
53	## Relay and adapter selection
54	
55	`[remote]` requires `adapter` and `prefix`. Sizes accept strings such as `50GB`
56	or `3900MiB`. Optional `part_size` controls splitting; defaults depend on the
57	adapter. `min_free` is enforced only when the adapter can report free space.
58	`max_inflight` limits outstanding payload bytes tracked for the job; allow at
59	least the largest whole unit, or sending can wait indefinitely.
60	
61	| Adapter | Main `options` | Requirements and limits |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| `local` | `root` | Existing directory; no backend CLI. Both sides must see the same relay contents. |
64	| `baidupcs` | `binary`, `upload_threads`, `download_threads` | Authenticated BaiduPCS-Go; default parts are 3900 MiB, download threads 4. |
65	| `rclone` | `remote`, `flags`, `endpoints` | Configured rclone remote, e.g. `gdrive:`. Set endpoint hostnames if inference fails. |
66	| `ghrelease` | `repo`, `tag` | Authenticated `gh`; creates a missing draft release and refuses a published one. Default parts 1900 MiB, each strictly below 2 GiB. |
67	| `rsync` | `host`, `root`, `ssh_options`, `flags` | rsync and, for a remote host, working noninteractive SSH; empty `host` means local. |
68	
69	Ferry requires non-empty remote objects and uses its own SHA-256 verification,
70	not backend checksums. Backend quotas and permissions still apply.
71	
72	`[remote.sides.sender]` and `[remote.sides.receiver]` can override `adapter` and
73	`options`. An overridden options table **replaces**, rather than merges with,
74	the base options. For direct SSH delivery, send via rsync and receive locally:
75	
76	```toml
77	[remote]
78	adapter = "rsync"
79	prefix = "/inbox"
80	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
81	
82	[remote.sides.receiver]
83	adapter = "local"
84	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
85	```
86	
87	This is a fragment, not a complete job. The receiver runs on `nas` and reads the
88	same landing directory. `egress = "direct"` is the default; see
89	[egress controls](operations.md#egress) before accepting proxy routes.
90	
91	## Example jobs
92	
93	Adapt paths and review policies before using these public repository examples:
94	
95	- [Incremental mirror](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/mirror-incremental.toml): retains sources and extracts at the destination.
96	- [Baidu archive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/daily-archive-baidu.toml): **deletes sources after remote size checks**; change to `never` for a pilot.
97	- [Google Drive](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/gdrive-via-proxy.toml): explicitly accepts non-direct egress.
98	- [GitHub draft release](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry/blob/main/examples/github-draft-release.toml): raw-file units; replace the repository placeholder.
99
````

````text
1	# Operations
2	
3	## Inspect before transferring
4	
5	```sh
6	ferry doctor job.toml
7	ferry doctor job.toml --side receiver
8	ferry plan job.toml
9	ferry status job.toml
10	ferry status job.toml --side receiver --json
11	ferry status job.toml --scan-source --remote
12	```
13	
14	Doctor checks the selected backend and egress; it can contact remote services
15	and, for rsync, create a missing landing directory. It is not a generic dry-run
16	or proof that every later backend operation will succeed. Plan enumerates source
17	units and members; it does not simulate transfer, settling, or source deletion.
18	
19	Status normally reads local ledgers. `--scan-source` adds source enumeration;
20	`--remote` queries the backend for relay information. Sender and receiver have
21	separate state, so inspect each on its own host. Commands accept `--json`, but
22	service output remains supervisor text rather than a general JSON report.
23	
24	## Run and resume
25	
26	```sh
27	ferry send job.toml
28	ferry receive job.toml --once
29	```
30	
31	Send processes eligible work and marks the sender done. Receive with `--once`
32	makes one pass; without it, receive waits until the sender is done and the relay
33	is empty. For continuous operation, run `send --follow` and `receive --follow`
34	in separate processes, adding `--poll 60` to control idle polling in seconds.
35	
36	To resume, restart the same command with the same job, state, staging, and relay
37	prefix. Do not delete ledgers, staged manifests, or destination partial files to
38	"fix" an interrupted transfer. Uploaded parts with matching remote sizes can be
39	reused; downloaded parts are checked by SHA-256 before reuse. One sender and one
40	receiver may run per job on a host; a second instance of either side fails fast.
41	
42	Inspect `<state_dir>/sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`, and side logs when progress
43	stalls. Check read windows, settling, staging space, remote limits, destination
44	free space, and preflight errors. Keep credentials and session files out of reports.
45	
46	## Integrity and destination safety
47	
48	The sender hashes the packed payload and its parts. The receiver checks sizes,
49	part and whole-payload SHA-256 hashes, and tar member counts before recording
50	verification. It then removes that unit's relay data. With extraction enabled,
51	existing unit paths are replaced, including removal of files absent in the new copy.
52	
53	Change detection is weaker than transfer verification: its path-and-size
54	fingerprints miss same-size edits. `ferry inventory job.toml --no-upload --json`
55	previews fingerprints of an existing destination tree; omit `--no-upload` only
56	when you intend to publish them to the relay for sender-side skipping. Use
57	`--root PATH` for a source-shaped tree when `receiver.dest` contains a key template.
58	Inventory seeding is not a content-hash audit or evidence of a fresh transfer.
59	
60	## Source deletion
61	
62	- `never` is the default and the recommended starting point.
63	- `after_remote_size` deletes source members after upload size checks, **before
64	  destination SHA-256 verification**. Use only for independently recoverable data.
65	- `after_receiver_ack` waits for the receiver's verification acknowledgement.
66	  Keep the sender running or restart it to consume acknowledgements; one-shot
67	  sending can wait for the receiver rather than exiting immediately.
68	
69	Keep source units immutable throughout transfer and acknowledgement handling:
70	settling does not lock files, and deletion acts on source paths. Use trusted,
71	job-specific relay storage; do not fabricate acknowledgements or reuse old
72	protocol state for a different dataset. Neither deletion policy replaces backups.
73	
74	## Egress
75	
76	Backend subprocesses always have proxy environment variables stripped, including
77	when `egress = "any"`. The default `direct` policy rejects detected backend proxy
78	settings, fake-IP DNS in `198.18.0.0/15`, and routes through recognized tunnel
79	interfaces. Backend-internal proxy configuration and host routing still matter.
80	
81	Set `remote.egress = "any"`, or pass `--allow-proxy` to doctor/send/receive, only
82	when accepting those egress findings is intentional. This does not restore proxy
83	environment variables or fix missing authentication. `trusted_interfaces` exempts
84	interfaces you have independently verified route this backend directly. Host
85	checks cannot detect every transparent upstream proxy; verify cost-sensitive paths.
86	
87	## Unattended operation
88	
89	Preview a supervisor definition before installing anything:
90	
91	```sh
92	ferry service job.toml --side receiver
93	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
94	```
95	
96	Systemd user units run follow mode with `Restart=on-failure`; cron uses one-shot
97	commands and job locks prevent overlap. `--install` writes and enables the selected
98	service, so it can start transfers immediately; `--uninstall` removes it. Systemd
99	may need `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` to survive logout. On other supervisors,
100	including launchd, use the corresponding send/receive command explicitly. Test
101	manually with source retention before enabling any unattended destructive policy.
102
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Getting started
2	
3	## Install
4	
5	With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed and Python 3.11+ available:
6	
7	```sh
8	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry
9	ferry --help
10	```
11	
12	Ensure uv's tool executable directory is on your `PATH`. The local adapter needs
13	no other tools or cloud account. Other adapters require their backend CLI and
14	separately configured authentication; never paste credential or session files
15	into a job, diagnostic report, or issue.
16	
17	## Try an isolated local relay
18	
19	Run these commands in one POSIX shell. They create a fresh temporary directory
20	containing a non-empty sample file, job state, staging, relay, and destination.
21	No existing dataset or cloud service is involved.
22	
23	```sh
24	demo=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ferry-demo.XXXXXX)
25	mkdir -p "$demo/source" "$demo/relay" "$demo/destination"
26	printf 'Hello from Ferry\n' > "$demo/source/hello.txt"
27	
28	cat > "$demo/job.toml" <<EOF
29	name = "local-demo"
30	state_dir = "$demo/state"
31	
32	[units]
33	root = "$demo/source"
34	glob = "*.txt"
35	pack = "none"
36	
37	[sender]
38	stage_dir = "$demo/stage"
39	delete_source = "never"
40	
41	[receiver]
42	dest = "$demo/destination"
43	extract = false
44	
45	[remote]
46	adapter = "local"
47	prefix = "/local-demo"
48	egress = "direct"
49	options = { root = "$demo/relay" }
50	EOF
51	
52	ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml"
53	ferry doctor "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
54	ferry plan "$demo/job.toml"
55	ferry send "$demo/job.toml"
56	ferry receive "$demo/job.toml" --once
57	ferry status "$demo/job.toml" --side receiver
58	cmp "$demo/source/hello.txt" "$demo/destination/hello.txt"
59	printf 'Demo directory: %s\n' "$demo"
60	```
61	
62	Both doctor checks should report `OK`; plan and receiver status should each show
63	one unit. `cmp` exits successfully without output when files match. The source
64	remains intact; verified relay payloads are removed, but protocol files may remain.
65	Keep the printed directory to inspect or repeat the job: using the same state
66	resumes recorded work rather than forcing a fresh copy. The demo directory remains.
67	
68	## Move to two hosts
69	
70	Use matching job names, unit definitions, and relay prefixes, with host-appropriate
71	paths and persistent state on each host. Start with a small disposable dataset and
72	`delete_source = "never"`; run doctor for each side before sending.
73	Choose a backend in [Configuration](configuration.md), then read
74	[Operations](operations.md) before enabling follow mode or source deletion.
75
````
</details></tool-use>

## Recommended implementation plan

### 1. Add a small, offline configuration wizard

Introduce `ferry init [--output PATH] [--stdout]`, defaulting to `job.toml`.

- Register `init` separately from job-based commands; dispatch it **before** `main()` calls `load_job()`.
- Keep prompts, validation, TOML rendering, and saving in one new wizard module with injectable input/output for tests.
- Require interactive stdin. Non-TTY invocation exits 2 with guidance to use documented TOML examples; `--help` always works.
- Send prompts and diagnostics to stderr. With `--stdout`, emit only the completed TOML to stdout and write nothing. Clearly label accompanying service commands as requiring the proposed configuration to be saved first.
- Correct the CLI’s blanket claim that every command provides JSON; do not introduce a wizard JSON interface.

**Prompt sequence**

1. Job name, source root, persistent state/staging paths.
2. Unit selection: `glob` or `keys_from` plus member templates; packing choice.
3. Receiver destination and extraction choice, explaining replacement behavior.
4. Backend and minimal non-secret settings:
   - Local: relay root.
   - BaiduPCS: executable; authentication remains external.
   - Rclone: configured remote name.
   - GitHub releases: repository and draft-release tag.

1	# Ferry
2	
3	Ferry moves bulk data between disconnected hosts through cloud storage or a
4	shared directory. With SSH connectivity, it can use an rsync landing directory.
5	The Python 3.11+ CLI has no runtime Python dependencies; cloud and SSH adapters
6	use separately installed backend tools.
7	
8	## How transfers work
9	
10	A job groups source paths into **units**: tar archives or raw files, split into
11	parts if needed. The sender uploads parts, then `manifest.json` to mark readiness.
12	The receiver verifies sizes and SHA-256, places the result, and removes relay data.
13	
14	- Resume uses per-host ledgers, sender staging, and verified receiver parts.
15	- Read windows and space limits help control source load and relay occupancy.
16	- Follow mode discovers new units and detects some source changes.
17	
18	**The relay is temporary transport, not a backup.** Use dedicated relay and
19	destination paths, retain sources with `delete_source = "never"`, and verify
20	recovery before considering automatic source deletion.
21	
22	## CLI workflow
23	
24	```mermaid
25	flowchart TD
26	    accTitle: Ferry command-line workflow
27	    accDescr: Create a source-preserving job, check both sides, plan units, run sender and receiver on their hosts, then inspect status or resume using the same state.
28	    Setup["Install tools<br/>Create job.toml"] --> Doctor["ferry doctor<br/>Check both sides"]
29	    Doctor --> Plan["Resolve findings<br/>ferry plan"]
30	    Plan --> Transfer
31	    subgraph Transfer["Separate terminals / hosts"]
32	        direction LR
33	        Send["ferry send"] -. "Parts + manifest" .-> Receive["ferry receive<br/>Verify SHA-256"]
34	    end
35	    Transfer --> Status["ferry status<br/>Inspect each side"]
36	    Status --> Continue{"Interrupted?"}
37	    Continue -- "Restart" --> Resume["Reuse job and state"]
38	    Resume --> Transfer
39	    Continue -- "No" --> Inspect["Monitor or finish<br/>Retain source by default"]
40	```
41	
42	Run sender and receiver in separate terminals or on their respective hosts;
43	you do not need to wait for sending to finish before receiving. In particular,
44	`after_receiver_ack` can keep the sender waiting for receiver verification.
45	Use `--once` only when one receiver pass is intended. For continuous jobs, start
46	both sides with `--follow` and leave those processes running rather than starting
47	duplicate senders or receivers. See
48	[Operations](operations.md) for preflight side effects, follow mode, source
49	deletion policies, and destination replacement behavior.
50	
51	| Stage | What to do |
52	|---|---|
53	| Prepare | Install the required tools and write a job from a reviewed example. |
54	| Inspect | Run doctor for both sides, resolve findings, then review the source units with plan. |
55	| Transfer | Run send and receive on the correct hosts with matching job/relay settings. |
56	| Monitor | Read each side's status on its own host; verification happens inside receive. |
57	| Resume | Reuse the same job, ledgers, staging and relay prefix; do not delete state to restart. |
58	
59	## Start here
60	
61	1. [Getting started](getting-started.md): install and try an isolated local relay.
62	2. [Configuration](configuration.md): define units, limits, and backend adapters.
63	3. [Operations](operations.md): inspect progress, resume, and run unattended.

1. Job 名稱、來源根目錄、持久化 state／staging 路徑。
2. 每個檔案／資料夾一個 unit，或進階的 `keys_from + members` 分組；tar 或單一原始檔。
3. Receiver 目的地、是否解壓；說明解壓會替換目的地中的相應 unit 路徑。
4. Backend 與必要非機密參數：

   - `rclone`：已設定的 remote 名稱。

5. Job 專用 remote prefix。
6. 本機執行 sender／receiver，以及手動、systemd、cron 或 pueue；預設手動。

第一版處理常見配置，不把所有調校選項複製成第二份 schema；進階容量、時窗與刪除政策連至 configuration 文件。明寫安全預設：`delete_source = "never"`、`egress = "direct"`、`extract = false`。跨主機路徑必須標明屬於哪一端；不要求遠端目錄在目前機器存在，也不將遠端 `~` 誤展開成本機 home。

### 安全與驗證邊界

- 重用 `src/ferry/job.py` 的 `job_from_dict()` 及現有 size/window parsers（有提示對應欄位時），不另造一般設定解析器。
- 固定 schema TOML renderer 正確處理字串 escaping、Unicode、bool、arrays 與 nested tables；先經 `tomllib.loads()` round-trip，再呼叫 `job_from_dict()`。
- Backend 選項只做本地必要欄位檢查。**不呼叫 `make_adapter()`、doctor、登入或傳輸**；rsync adapter 建構本身可能執行 SSH 查詢。
- 不讀取、輸出或收集 backend credentials／session 檔案。
- 需要互動 stdin；非 TTY 回傳 2 並指向範例，不掛住等待輸入。`--help` 不受限制。
- Prompts／診斷送 stderr；`--stdout` 僅輸出完成的 TOML、不寫檔，後續指令需註明先儲存至所選路徑。
- 既有目標（含 symlink）一律拒絕覆寫，第一版無 `--force`；要求 parent 已存在，確認後 exclusive create。寫入失败只清理由本次建立的未完成檔案。
- EOF 回傳 2、Ctrl-C 回傳 130，無 traceback；確認前取消不產生檔案。
- 修正 CLI「每個 command 都有 JSON」的過度概括；wizard 不新增 JSON 介面。

## 2. 串接既有 systemd／cron 功能

重用 `src/ferry/service.py` 的 `systemd_unit()`、`cron_line()` 與 `command()`：
- Systemd 選項顯示既有 follow-mode unit 與正確 shell-quoted 的安裝命令。
- Cron 選項詢問 schedule，顯示 cron entry 與安裝命令；拒絕換行等會產生多筆設定的输入。
- Pueue 選項提供使用指南與適合所選 side 的提示，不啟動 daemon 或提交工作。
- **Wizard 不安裝、不 enable、不啟動任何服務。** 實際安裝仍是使用者明確執行既有 `ferry service … --install`，移除使用 `--uninstall`。
- 將 `src/ferry/cli.py` 的 `linger_enabled()` 查詢移至 systemd 安裝分支；單純預覽改為靜態 linger 說明，不執行 `loginctl`。
- 不自動啟用 linger、不加 sudo、不加入新的直接 subprocess 呼叫；不擴大為既有 service subprocess plumbing 的全面重構。

文件清楚列出現有指令，例如：

```sh
ferry service /absolute/job.toml --side receiver
ferry service /absolute/job.toml --side receiver --install
ferry service /absolute/job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
ferry service /absolute/job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
```

## 3. 英文文件與 pueue 推薦流程

修改：
- `docs/getting-started.md`：新增 wizard walkthrough，保留可重現的手寫 local demo。
- `docs/configuration.md`：說明 wizard 覆蓋範圍、安全預設、外部認證及 host-specific 路徑。
- `docs/operations.md`：補完整預覽／安裝／移除、backend PATH、非互動登入、systemd linger／logs、cron 重疊回傳 2，以及安裝可能立即開始傳輸的說明。
- 新增 `docs/pueue.md`；從 `docs/index.md`、operations 及 `README.md` 連入。保留 `zensical.toml` 的自動導覽和英文設定，不改 CI／部署設定。

### pueue 指南必須涵蓋

1. **主要推薦**：receiver 由 service manager 執行 `receive --follow`；sender 的非 follow 批次由 pueue 排隊。Sender 即使非 follow，仍可能因重試、讀取時窗、容量或 ACK 等待而長時間不結束。
2. 使用公開 `pueue` CLI：建立 dedicated group、設定 parallelism、`--label`、`--escape`、`--print-task-id`，以及 status／log／restart。無需安裝 repo 的 agent skill scripts。
3. ACK／relay 背壓情境下，**不可將 receiver 設為 sender 的 `--after`，也不可讓兩端共用只有一個 slot 的 queue**。同一 job/side 不要同時交由 pueue 與 service 管理；鎖是本機限制，不是跨主機分散式鎖。
4. 成功後串行 receive 的示範僅用於可完整放進 relay、保留來源的小型靜態批次；不要當一般推薦流程。
5. `receive --once` 只掃一輪；缺 manifest 或空間不足可能跳過工作。一般 receive 也可能被先前批次留下的 done marker 提前結束；重複批次優先持續 receiver。
6. `pueue wait` 完成／程序 exit 0 不保證資料全部交付；查看 Ferry receiver status／ledger，必要時比對預期資料。說明 SIGTERM 目前可能在未完成時回傳 0。
7. 重試保留 job、state、staging、relay；`restart` 預設新增 task，`--in-place` 會覆寫舊 log。
8. 在實際執行主機提交（需要時 SSH 進去）；task ID 屬於該 daemon，不能跨主機依賴。
9. 分清背景執行、重開機恢復及週期排程：pueue 持久化 queue 不等於自動續跑中斷程序；cron／timer 管週期，systemd 管常駐服務。不假設舊 Linux 一定可使用 systemd user manager。

將已確認的 stale done marker 與中止 exit status 問題記入 `TODO.md`，此變更僅文件提醒，不更改傳輸生命週期／協定。

1	"""Any rclone remote (Google Drive, S3, OneDrive, ...).
2	
3	``options.remote`` is the rclone remote with optional base path, e.g. ``"gdrive:"`` or
4	``"s3:bucket/relay"``. rclone honours proxy environment variables, which the egress guard
5	strips; endpoints for the route check come from ``options.endpoints`` or are inferred
6	from the remote's backend type.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import json
11	import shutil
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	from ..proc import CommandError, run, run_transfer
15	from .base import Adapter
16	
17	_BACKEND_ENDPOINTS = {
18	    "drive": ("www.googleapis.com",),
19	    "onedrive": ("graph.microsoft.com",),
20	    "dropbox": ("api.dropboxapi.com", "content.dropboxapi.com"),
21	    "box": ("api.box.com", "upload.box.com"),
22	    "b2": ("api.backblazeb2.com",),
23	}
24	
25	
26	class RcloneAdapter(Adapter):
27	    name = "rclone"
28	
29	    def __init__(self, options: dict, log: Path | None = None):
30	        super().__init__(options, log)
31	        self.bin = options.get("binary") or shutil.which("rclone") or "rclone"
32	        self.remote = options["remote"]
33	        if ":" not in self.remote:
34	            raise ValueError("rclone remote must look like 'name:' or 'name:path'")
35	        self.flags = list(options.get("flags", []))
36	        self.endpoints = tuple(options.get("endpoints") or self._infer_endpoints())
37	
38	    def _infer_endpoints(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
39	        name = self.remote.split(":", 1)[0]
40	        try:
41	            remotes = run([self.bin, "listremotes", "--long"], timeout=60)
42	        except (OSError, CommandError):
43	            return ()
44	        for line in remotes.splitlines():
45	            parts = line.split()
46	            if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[0] == f"{name}:":
47	                return _BACKEND_ENDPOINTS.get(parts[1], ())
48	        return ()
49	
50	    def _full(self, remote: str) -> str:
51	        base = self.remote if self.remote.endswith(":") else self.remote.rstrip("/") + "/"
52	        return base + remote.lstrip("/")
53	
54	    def check(self) -> list[str]:
55	        if not shutil.which(self.bin) and not Path(self.bin).is_file():
56	            return [f"rclone not found ({self.bin})"]
57	        problems = []
58	        if not self.endpoints:
59	            problems.append("rclone endpoints unknown; set remote.options.endpoints "
60	                            "so the egress guard can check routes")
61	        return problems
62	
63	    def put(self, local: Path, remote: str) -> None:
64	        run_transfer([self.bin, "copyto", *self.flags, str(local), self._full(remote)],
65	                     log=self.log)

3	BaiduPCS-Go exits 0 even when the server reports an error (e.g. code 31066, "file or
4	directory does not exist"), so results are parsed from its output and every transfer is
5	verified by size afterwards. Reported MD5s are unreliable and never used.
6	Login/session state lives in BaiduPCS-Go's own config and is never read here.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import os
11	import posixpath
12	import re
13	import shutil
14	import tempfile
15	from pathlib import Path
16	
17	from ..proc import run, run_transfer
18	from .base import Adapter
19	
20	_UNIT = {"B": 1, "KB": 1024, "MB": 1024**2, "GB": 1024**3, "TB": 1024**4, "PB": 1024**5}
21	_LS_ROW = re.compile(
22	    r"^\s*\d+\s+(?:-|[\d.]+[KMGTP]?B)\s+\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\s{2}(.+?)\s*$")
23	_MISSING = ("31066", "不存在")
24	
25	
26	def parse_quota(text: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
27	    def grab(label: str) -> int | None:
28	        m = re.search(label + r":\s*([\d.]+)\s*([KMGTP]?B)", text)
29	        return int(float(m.group(1)) * _UNIT[m.group(2)]) if m else None
30	
31	    total, used = grab("总空间"), grab("已用空间")
32	    return (total, used) if total is not None and used is not None else None
33	
34	
35	def parse_meta_size(text: str) -> int | None:
36	    if any(s in text for s in _MISSING):
37	        return None
38	    if re.search(r"类型\s+目录", text):
39	        return None
40	    m = re.search(r"文件大小\s+(\d+),", text)
41	    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None
42	
43	
44	def parse_ls(text: str) -> list[str]:
45	    if any(s in text for s in _MISSING):
46	        return []
47	    return [m.group(1) for line in text.splitlines() if (m := _LS_ROW.match(line))]
48	
49	
50	def parse_config_value(text: str, key: str) -> str:
51	    """Value column of ``BaiduPCS-Go config`` (name, value, [range], description)."""
52	    for line in text.splitlines():
53	        cols = re.split(r"\s{2,}", line.strip())
54	        if cols and cols[0] == key:
55	            return cols[1] if len(cols) >= 3 else ""
56	    return ""
