1	# ferry
2	
3	Resumable bulk transfer between hosts that cannot reach each other, relayed through cloud
4	storage (Baidu Pan, any rclone remote, a GitHub draft release, or a shared directory) — or
5	directly over ssh with rsync when the hosts can reach each other.
6	
7	```
8	source host                         relay                          destination host
9	ferry send  ── pack ─▶ stage ─ push ─▶  prefix/<key>/part-*   ─ pull ─▶ verify ─▶ dest
10	                                         prefix/<key>/manifest.json  (READY, uploaded last)
11	```
12	
13	- **Units**: one key = one tar (or one raw file) = one remote directory. Resume is per unit
14	  and per part; nothing is re-uploaded after a restart.
15	- **Integrity**: sha256 is computed while packing (single source read). The receiver checks
16	  every part, the reassembled payload and the tar member count. Backend checksums (e.g.
17	  Baidu MD5) are never trusted.
18	- **Backpressure**: staging cap on the sender, remote free-space floor and in-flight limit,
19	  so a small relay can move a much larger dataset.
20	- **Read windows**: packing (the heavy source read) can be blocked in given hours, e.g.
21	  `"Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"`; uploads continue from staging.
22	- **Direct egress by default**: proxy variables are stripped from every backend process,
23	  backend-internal proxy settings are rejected, and endpoints resolving to clash/mihomo
24	  fake-ip or routed via a tun interface fail the preflight. See *Egress* below.
25	- **Source deletion policy**: `never`, `after_remote_size` (as soon as the relay holds a
26	  byte-identical-size copy; for regenerable data) or `after_receiver_ack` (after the
27	  destination verified sha256).
28	
29	## Documentation
30	
31	Read the [English documentation](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/ferry/) for a safe
32	local quickstart, configuration reference, and operational guidance. The
33	[Markdown sources](docs/index.md) are also available in this repository.
34	
35	GitHub Actions checks documentation on pull requests and deploys the Zensical
36	site to GitHub Pages after documentation changes reach `main`. The workflow can
37	also be run manually on `main` to rebuild and deploy the site.
38	
39	```bash
40	just docs-setup   # install the locked docs group alongside dev dependencies
41	just docs-build   # strict site build plus HTML/Markdown/LLM artifact checks
42	just docs-serve              # http://127.0.0.1:8000
43	just docs-serve 8769         # use another port if 8000 is occupied
44	just docs-serve 8769 0.0.0.0 # optional: expose preview on all interfaces
45	```
46	
47	`docs-serve` takes an optional port followed by an optional host. Keep the
48	loopback default unless network access is intentional; binding `0.0.0.0` exposes
49	the preview to other hosts allowed by your firewall. Do not stop another service
50	just to reclaim port 8000.
51	
52	Documentation tooling is not part of ferry's runtime dependencies.
53	
54	## Install
55	
56	```bash
57	uv tool install git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry   # CLI on PATH
58	# or as a dependency:  ferry @ git+https://github.com/daviddwlee84/ferry@v0.1.0
59	```
60	
61	Python ≥ 3.11, no runtime dependencies. Backend CLIs are used as installed:
62	[BaiduPCS-Go](https://github.com/qjfoidnh/BaiduPCS-Go), `rclone`, `gh`.
63	
64	## Job file
65	
66	```toml
67	name = "daily-archive"                        # also the default state dir name
68	# state_dir = "~/.local/state/ferry/<name>"   # ledgers, logs, lock
69	
70	[units]
71	root = "/data/shared/dataset"
72	keys_from = "_manifests/*.json"               # key = file stem / dir name
73	members = ["order/{key}", "trans/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json"]
74	# or: glob = "exports/*.parquet"  (each match is a unit); pack = "none" sends files as-is
75	settle = "6h"                                 # skip units with files newer than this
76	resend_changed = true                         # re-send units whose fingerprint changed
77	recheck_recent = 30                           # after the first pass, recheck newest 30 keys
78	
79	[sender]
80	stage_dir = "~/.cache/ferry/daily-archive"
81	stage_cap = "300GB"
82	read_blocked = ["Mon-Fri 09:15-15:30 Asia/Shanghai"]
83	delete_source = "after_remote_size"           # never | after_remote_size | after_receiver_ack
84	
85	[receiver]
86	dest = "/srv/archive/dataset/{key[0:4]}"      # {key} and slices like {key[0:4]}
87	# extract = true                              # unpack; each unit path is replaced whole
88	# min_free = "20GB"                           # wait while the destination is this full
89	
90	[remote]
91	adapter = "baidupcs"                          # local | baidupcs | rclone | ghrelease
92	prefix = "/ferry/daily-archive"
93	part_size = "3900MiB"                         # default per adapter
94	min_free = "200GB"
95	max_inflight = "1.5TB"
96	egress = "direct"                             # direct | any
97	# trusted_interfaces = ["Meta"]               # TUN you verified routes this backend DIRECT
98	options = { download_threads = 4 }
99	```
100	
101	Adapter options:
102	
103	| adapter | options |
104	|---|---|
105	| `local` | `root` (directory used as relay) |
106	| `baidupcs` | `binary` (default: PATH or `~/.local/bin/BaiduPCS-Go`), `upload_threads`, `download_threads` (4) |
107	| `rclone` | `remote` (`"gdrive:"`, `"s3:bucket/relay"`), `flags`, `endpoints` (route check hosts) |
108	| `ghrelease` | `repo` (`owner/name`), `tag` (draft release, created if missing; refuses a published release) |
109	| `rsync` | `host` (ssh alias; `""` = local), `root` (landing dir on that host), `ssh_options`, `flags` |
110	
111	`[remote.sides.sender]` / `[remote.sides.receiver]` override `adapter` and `options` for one
112	side. Direct mode uses this: the sender pushes with `rsync` into a landing directory on the
113	destination host, and the receiver there reads the same directory with `local`:
114	
115	```toml
116	[remote]
117	adapter = "rsync"
118	prefix = "/inbox"
119	options = { host = "nas", root = "/srv/landing" }
120	[remote.sides.receiver]
121	adapter = "local"
122	options = { root = "/srv/landing" }
123	```
124	
125	Compared with plain `rsync -a`, this adds read windows, many-small-files packing, sha256
126	verification of every unit, source-deletion policies, ledgers with throughput/ETA, and
127	change detection for long-running mirrors.
128	
129	## Backfill and increments are the same job
130	
131	A job with `delete_source = "never"` mirrors a growing, occasionally repaired source:
132	
133	- **First run = backfill**: every unit not yet sent is packed and sent.
134	- **`--follow` = increments**: new keys are picked up; units still being written are held
135	  back by `settle`.
136	- **Repairs**: each unit has a fingerprint (sorted relative paths + sizes; stat only). A
137	  changed unit is re-sent as a new revision; with `extract = true` the receiver replaces
138	  each unit path wholesale, so files deleted at the source disappear too. After the first
139	  pass only the newest `recheck_recent` keys are re-fingerprinted each round; restart the
140	  sender (or run without `--follow`) for a full recheck.
141	- **Seeding**: if the destination already holds part of the data, run
142	  `ferry inventory job.toml` on the receiver. It publishes fingerprints of what it has;
143	  the sender marks identical units as `seeded` instead of sending them.
144	
145	## Commands
146	
147	```bash
148	ferry doctor job.toml [--side receiver]   # backend login, proxy settings, routes
149	ferry plan job.toml                       # units found under the source root
150	ferry send job.toml [--follow]            # until every unit is pushed (then marks done)
151	ferry receive job.toml [--once|--follow]  # until the sender is done and the relay is empty
152	ferry inventory job.toml [--root PATH]     # receiver: publish fingerprints for seeding
153	ferry status job.toml [--side receiver] [--scan-source] [--remote] [--json]
154	```
155	
156	A second sender (or receiver) for the same job on the same host exits immediately.
157	
158	### Running unattended
159	
160	ferry has no daemon of its own: `send`/`receive --follow` is a long-running loop that
161	polls for new or changed units. Put it under a supervisor; `ferry service` prints (or,
162	with `--install`, writes and enables) one:
163	
164	```bash
165	ferry service job.toml --side receiver                 # print a systemd user unit
166	ferry service job.toml --side receiver --install       # ~/.config/systemd/user/ferry-<job>-receiver.service
167	ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
168	ferry service job.toml --side sender --uninstall
169	loginctl enable-linger $USER                           # let user services run without a login
170	```
171	
172	systemd units run `--follow` with `Restart=on-failure`; cron entries run one-shot
173	(`send`, `receive --once`) and rely on the job lock to skip overlapping runs. Any other
174	supervisor (pueue, tmux, launchd) works the same way: run the printed command.
175	
176	Library use (e.g. from an orchestrator):
177	
178	```python
179	import ferry
180	job = ferry.load_job("job.toml")
181	report = ferry.preflight(job, ferry.adapter_for(job, "sender"))
182	result = ferry.send(job)            # SendResult(pushed=..., pushed_bytes=..., ...)
183	st = ferry.side_status(job, "sender", remote=True)
184	```
185	
186	## Egress
187	
188	Proxy traffic is metered, so by default ferry insists on a direct path:
189	
190	1. `http(s)_proxy`, `all_proxy`, ... are removed from every backend process environment.
191	2. Backend tools' own proxy settings (BaiduPCS-Go `proxy`) are reported.
192	3. Each backend endpoint is resolved; a `198.18.0.0/15` answer (clash/mihomo fake-ip DNS)
193	   or a route via `tun*`/`utun*`/`Meta`/`wg*`/`tailscale*` is reported.
194	
195	With `egress = "direct"` any finding fails `send`/`receive`; `egress = "any"` (or
196	`--allow-proxy` for one run) accepts them with warnings — for backends that are only
197	reachable through a proxy, e.g. Google Drive from mainland China, where the proxy's own
198	rules may still pick DIRECT for some hosts. A transparent proxy on the router is not
199	visible from the host and cannot be detected.
200	
201	## Backend notes
202	
203	See [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — e.g. Baidu silently drops empty files and exits 0 on
204	errors, single-threaded Baidu downloads are ~4x slower, GitHub assets are limited to 2 GiB.
205
````
</details></tool-use>

121	def remove_inside(root: Path, rel: str) -> None:
122	    """Delete root/rel, refusing anything that resolves outside root."""
123	    target = (root / rel)
124	    resolved = target.resolve()
125	    if not resolved.is_relative_to(root.resolve()) or resolved == root.resolve():
126	        raise PreflightError(f"refusing to delete {target}: outside source root")
127	    if target.is_dir() and not target.is_symlink():

DOCS = "https://daviddwlee84.github.io/ferry/"


class Prompts:
    def __init__(self, stdin: TextIO, stderr: TextIO):
        self.stdin = stdin
        self.stderr = stderr

    def say(self, text: str) -> None:
        print(text, file=self.stderr)

    def ask(self, label: str, default: str | None = None,
            validate: Callable[[str], str] | None = None) -> str:
        while True:
            suffix = f" [{default}]" if default is not None else ""
            print(f"{label}{suffix}: ", end="", file=self.stderr, flush=True)
            line = self.stdin.readline()
            if not line:
                raise EOFError
            value = line.strip() or default
            try:
                if value is None:
                    raise ValueError("a value is required")
                if any(ord(c) < 32 or ord(c) == 127 for c in value):
                    raise ValueError("use a single line without control characters")
                return validate(value) if validate else value
            except ValueError as e:
                self.say(f"Invalid input: {e}")

    def choice(self, label: str, options: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...], default: str) -> str:
        self.say(label)
        for i, (key, description) in enumerate(options, 1):
            self.say(f"  {i}. {key}: {description}")
        keys = [key for key, _ in options]

        def select(value: str) -> str:
            value = value.lower()
            if value in keys:
                return value
            if value.isdecimal() and 1 <= int(value) <= len(keys):
                return keys[int(value) - 1]
            raise ValueError("choose a number or one of " + ", ".join(keys))

        return self.ask("Choice", default, select)

    def confirm(self, label: str, *, default: bool = False) -> bool:
        def yes_no(value: str) -> str:
            if value.lower() in ("y", "yes"):
                return "yes"
            if value.lower() in ("n", "no"):
                return "no"
            raise ValueError("answer yes or no")

        return self.ask(label, "yes" if default else "no", yes_no) == "yes"


def _name(value: str) -> str:
    if not _KEY.fullmatch(value):
        raise ValueError("use 1–128 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens; "
                         "start with a letter or digit")
    return value


def _host_path(value: str) -> str:
    if not (value.startswith("/") or value.startswith("~/")):
        raise ValueError("use an absolute path or ~/path on the host that will use it")
    return value


def _absolute_path(value: str) -> str:
    if not value.startswith("/"):
        raise ValueError("use an absolute path on that host")
    return value


def _relative_pattern(value: str) -> str:
    if value.startswith("/") or ".." in value.split("/"):
        raise ValueError("use a pattern relative to the source root, without '..'")
    return value


def _member(value: str) -> str:
    _relative_pattern(value)
    if "{" in value.replace("{key}", "") or "}" in value.replace("{key}", ""):
        raise ValueError("member templates support {key}, e.g. data/{key}")
    return value


def _destination(value: str) -> str:
    _host_path(value)
    literal = re.sub(r"\{key(?:\[-?\d*:-?\d*\])?\}", "", value)
    if "{" in literal or "}" in literal:
        raise ValueError("destination templates support {key} and slices like {key[0:4]}")
    return value


def _binary(value: str) -> str:
    if value.startswith("-") or ("/" in value and not value.startswith("/")):
        raise ValueError("use an executable name on PATH or an absolute executable path")
    return value


def _rclone_remote(value: str) -> str:
    name, colon, _ = value.partition(":")
    if not colon or not re.fullmatch(r"[\w .-]+", name):
        raise ValueError("use a configured remote, e.g. gdrive: or s3:bucket/relay; "
                         "do not enter credentials or on-the-fly remote definitions")
    return value


def _repo(value: str) -> str:
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", value) or value.startswith("-"):
        raise ValueError("use owner/repository, not a URL or access token")
    return value


def _ssh_host(value: str) -> str:
    if value.startswith("-") or any(c.isspace() for c in value):
        raise ValueError("use an SSH host alias or user@host, without command-line options")
    return value


def _prefix(value: str) -> str:
    if not value.startswith("/") or not value.strip("/") or ".." in value.split("/"):
        raise ValueError("use a dedicated absolute relay prefix, e.g. /ferry/my-job")
    return value.rstrip("/")


def _schedule(value: str) -> str:
    if len(value.split()) != 5 or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9*/?,#\-\s]+", value):
        raise ValueError("use five cron fields, e.g. '0 2 * * *' (without quotes)")
    return value


def collect(p: Prompts) -> dict:
    p.say("Create a source-preserving job. This does not contact backends or start transfers.\n"
          "Enter paths without shell quotes. Source paths belong to the sender; destination\n"
          "paths belong to the receiver. ~/ is expanded on the host using each path.\n"
          "Use separate, persistent state/staging and dedicated relay/destination directories.")
    name = p.ask("Job name", "my-job", _name)
    root = p.ask("Source root (sender host)", validate=_host_path)
    state = p.ask("State directory (local to each host)", f"~/.local/state/ferry/{name}",
                  _host_path)
    stage = p.ask("Staging directory (sender host)", f"{state.rstrip('/')}/stage", _host_path)
    units = {"root": root}
    selection = p.choice("How should paths be grouped into units?", (
        ("glob", "each matching file or directory is one unit"),
        ("keys", "collect several paths per key, e.g. a date")), "glob")
    if selection == "glob":
        units["glob"] = p.ask("Source-relative pattern (e.g. exports/*.parquet)", "*",
                              _relative_pattern)
    else:
        units["keys_from"] = p.ask("Key discovery pattern (file stem or directory name)",
                                   "_manifests/*.json", _relative_pattern)
        p.say("Enter one relative member template at a time, e.g. data/{key}.\n"
              "Missing members are omitted; review with ferry plan before sending.")
        members = [p.ask("Member template", validate=_member)]
        while value := p.ask("Another member template (blank finishes)", "", _member):
            members.append(value)
        units["members"] = members
    units["pack"] = p.choice("How should units be packed?", (
        ("tar", "archive a file, directory, or group (supports empty member files)"),
        ("none", "send one non-empty regular file per unit, unchanged")), "tar")
    dest = p.ask("Destination (receiver host; optional {key} or {key[0:4]})",
                 validate=_destination)
    extract = False
    if units["pack"] == "tar":
        p.say("Extraction replaces affected destination paths, including removing stale files.\n"
              "Leave it off to retain tar archives; use a dedicated destination either way.")
        extract = p.confirm("Extract archives at the destination?")
    adapter = p.choice("Which relay backend? Authentication must be configured separately.", (
        ("local", "shared/local directory; no backend CLI"),
        ("baidupcs", "Baidu Pan via authenticated BaiduPCS-Go"),
        ("rclone", "an existing configured rclone remote"),
        ("ghrelease", "GitHub draft release via authenticated gh"),
        ("rsync", "rsync landing directory, optionally over noninteractive SSH")), "local")
    options: dict = {}
    sides: dict = {}
    if adapter == "local":
        p.say("Both hosts must see the same relay contents (adjust root per host if needed).")
        options["root"] = p.ask("Relay root", validate=_host_path)
    elif adapter == "baidupcs":
        options["binary"] = p.ask("BaiduPCS-Go executable", "BaiduPCS-Go", _binary)
    elif adapter == "rclone":
        options["remote"] = p.ask("Configured remote (e.g. gdrive:)", validate=_rclone_remote)
        p.say("If endpoint inference fails, set remote.options.endpoints before running doctor.")
    elif adapter == "ghrelease":
        options["repo"] = p.ask("GitHub repository (owner/repository)", validate=_repo)
        options["tag"] = p.ask("Dedicated draft release tag", f"ferry-{name}")
        p.say("Ferry creates a missing draft during transfers and refuses published releases.")
    else:
        options["host"] = p.ask("SSH host (blank for a local landing directory)", "", _ssh_host)
        options["root"] = p.ask("Absolute landing root (on the target host)",
                                validate=_absolute_path)
        if options["host"] and p.confirm("Will the receiver run on that host and read locally?",
                                          default=True):
            sides["receiver"] = {"adapter": "local", "options": {"root": options["root"]}}
    remote = {"adapter": adapter, "prefix": p.ask("Dedicated relay prefix", f"/ferry/{name}",
                                                _prefix),
              "egress": "direct", "options": options}
    if sides:
        remote["sides"] = sides
    return {"name": name, "state_dir": state, "units": units,
            "sender": {"stage_dir": stage, "delete_source": "never"},
            "receiver": {"dest": dest, "extract": extract}, "remote": remote}


def _toml_value(value: str | bool | list) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        # JSON's Unicode scalar strings also work in TOML, except literal DEL.
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False).replace("\x7f", "\\u007f")
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "[" + ", ".join(_toml_value(item) for item in value) + "]"
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported wizard value: {type(value).__name__}")


def render(data: dict) -> str:
    """Render the wizard's fixed schema, not arbitrary TOML keys or value types."""
    lines = ["# Generated by ferry init; authentication stays in your backend tools."]

    def table(values: dict, prefix: str = "") -> None:
        if prefix:
            lines.extend(("", f"[{prefix}]"))
        for key, value in values.items():
            if not isinstance(value, dict):
                lines.append(f"{key} = {_toml_value(value)}")
        for key, value in values.items():
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                table(value, f"{prefix}.{key}" if prefix else key)

    table(data)
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def guidance(p: Prompts, job: Job) -> None:
    side = p.choice("Which side will run on this host?", (
        ("sender", "read, pack and upload source units"),
        ("receiver", "download and verify units")), "sender")
    method = p.choice("How will this side run? Nothing will be installed or started.", (
        ("manual", "print the command to run yourself"),
        ("systemd", "preview a Linux systemd user service"),
        ("cron", "preview a periodic crontab entry"),
        ("pueue", "show queue guidance; no task submission")), "manual")
    p.say("\nAfter saving, inspect the job and backend access explicitly:")
    p.say(shlex.join(["ferry", "doctor", str(job.path), "--side", side]))
    p.say("Doctor can contact the backend and, with rsync, create a landing directory.")
    if side == "sender":
        p.say(shlex.join(["ferry", "plan", str(job.path)]))
    if method in ("systemd", "cron"):
        args = ["ferry", "service", str(job.path), "--side", side, "--kind", method]
        if method == "systemd":
            p.say("\nSystemd preview (Linux; verify backend PATH/authentication and linger):")
            p.say(service.systemd_unit(job, side, poll=None))
        else:
            schedule = p.ask("Cron schedule (five fields)", "0 * * * *", _schedule)
            p.say("\nCrontab preview (single pass, not a guaranteed delivery deadline):")
            p.say(service.cron_line(job, side, schedule, poll=None))
            args += ["--schedule", schedule]
        p.say("Review first. This separate command installs the entry and may start transfers:")
        p.say(shlex.join([*args, "--install"]))
        p.say("To remove that entry later:")
        p.say(shlex.join([*args, "--uninstall"]))
    elif method == "pueue":
        p.say("\nUse a separately supervised receive --follow while queueing non-follow send.\n"
              "Do not queue a receiver after a sender that needs ACKs or relay space, or\n"
              "put both into a shared one-slot queue. Do not queue --follow in a finite chain.\n"
              "Do not let a service and pueue own the same job/side simultaneously.")
        if side == "sender":
            p.say("Queue this command on the sender host using the guide's labeled group setup:")
            p.say(shlex.join(service.command(job, side, follow=False, poll=None)))
        else:
            p.say("Keep the receiver running independently under a service manager:")
            p.say(shlex.join(service.command(job, side, follow=True, poll=None)))
        p.say(f"Guide: {DOCS}pueue/")
    else:
        p.say("\nRun explicitly when ready (receiver --once only scans once):")
        p.say(shlex.join(service.command(job, side, follow=False, poll=None)))
    p.say(f"Advanced limits, read windows and policies: {DOCS}configuration/\n"
          f"Supervision, resume and delivery checks: {DOCS}operations/")


def _write_new(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    created = None
    try:
        with path.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            created = os.fstat(f.fileno())
            f.write(text)
    except BaseException:
        if created is not None:
            try:
                current = path.lstat()
                if (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) == (created.st_dev, created.st_ino):
                    path.unlink()
            except OSError:
                pass
        raise


def run(output: str = "job.toml", *, to_stdout: bool = False,
        stdin: TextIO | None = None, stdout: TextIO | None = None,
        stderr: TextIO | None = None) -> int:
    stdin = sys.stdin if stdin is None else stdin
    stdout = sys.stdout if stdout is None else stdout
    stderr = sys.stderr if stderr is None else stderr
    p = Prompts(stdin, stderr)
    if not stdin.isatty():
        p.say(f"ferry init: interactive stdin is required; use a terminal or the TOML examples\n"
              f"at {DOCS}getting-started/. --stdout still requires interactive answers.")
        return 2
    try:
        path = Path(output).expanduser().absolute()
        if not to_stdout:
            if path.exists() or path.is_symlink():
                raise ValueError(f"refusing to overwrite {path}; choose a new --output path")
            if not path.parent.is_dir():
                raise ValueError(f"output parent directory does not exist: {path.parent}")
        data = collect(p)
        text = render(data)
        job = job_from_dict(tomllib.loads(text), path)
        p.say("\nConfiguration preview:\n" + text)
        if to_stdout:
            p.say(f"No file will be written. Save the TOML at {path} before using these commands.")
        guidance(p, job)
        action = "Print this configuration to stdout?" if to_stdout else f"Save to {path}?"
        if not p.confirm(action):
            p.say("Cancelled; no configuration written.")
            return 0
        if to_stdout:
            stdout.write(text)
        else:
            _write_new(path, text)
            p.say(f"Saved {path}. No transfer or service was started.")
        return 0
    except EOFError:
        p.say("\nferry init: input ended; setup cancelled.")
        return 2
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        p.say("\nferry init: interrupted; setup cancelled.")
        return 130
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        p.say(f"ferry init: {e}")
        return 2

```

# Pueue

[Pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) is an optional shell-task queue backed
by the `pueued` daemon. It can keep a submitted command running after you detach
from the terminal, label jobs, capture their output, and limit parallel tasks.
It is not a Ferry dependency, a distributed scheduler, or a replacement for
Ferry's integrity checks and resumable state.

The examples use Pueue 4.0.2 command syntax. Install Pueue separately and manage
`pueued` with the execution host's service manager; consult the
[upstream documentation](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki) for setup.
Ferry does not install or start it. Run `pueue status` to confirm your intended
daemon is reachable before submitting anything.

## Recommended arrangement

- **Receiver host:** a service-managed `ferry receive ... --follow` keeps draining
  the relay, verifying units, and publishing acknowledgements when required.
- **Sender host:** Pueue queues non-follow `ferry send ...` batches in a dedicated
  group with controlled concurrency.
- **Each job/side has one owner:** do not also install a sender service for the
  same queued sender, or run a second receiver while its service is active.

For continuous discovery on both sides, use service-managed `--follow` processes
instead of queue tasks expected to finish. Pueue groups limit the number of
whole Ferry processes, not Ferry's internal upload threads or parts.

A non-follow sender is a batch command, **not a bounded-duration command**. It
can wait indefinitely for upload retries, source read windows, staging/relay
capacity, or receiver acknowledgements. An apparently stuck Running task needs
Ferry diagnostics, not necessarily another queued copy.

## Prepare the receiver

On the receiver host, review the generated job, backend access, destination,
and [service environment](operations.md#environment-and-authentication). The
examples assume `name = "mirror"` and host-appropriate copies of the job.
Start with `delete_source = "never"`.

```sh
ferry doctor /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver
ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver
# Explicitly install and start the receiver after reviewing the preview.
ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --install
systemctl --user status ferry-mirror-receiver.service
```

Doctor can contact the backend; it is not an offline validation command.
Installation starts receiving immediately. On hosts without a usable systemd
user manager, run the receiver under an available service manager, or in a
separate foreground terminal for a supervised trial. Do not put that receiver
behind the sender in a queue dependency chain.

## Queue a sender batch

On the sender host, first inspect source units and backend access:

```sh
ferry doctor /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender
ferry plan /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml
```

Create the dedicated group once. Pueue does not create missing groups when you
submit a task; if the group already exists, inspect it rather than recreating it.

```sh
pueue group add ferry-send
pueue parallel 1 --group ferry-send
```

Submit from a stable working directory, using absolute executable and job paths:

```sh
cd "$HOME"
ferry_bin=$(command -v ferry)
job=/home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml

sender_id=$(pueue add --group ferry-send --label send-mirror-batch01 \
  --print-task-id --escape -- "$ferry_bin" send "$job")
printf 'Sender task: %s\n' "$sender_id"
```

Verify that `command -v ferry` returns an absolute executable path, not an alias
or shell function, before submitting. `--escape` preserves each argument,
including paths containing spaces. Without it, Pueue joins arguments into a
shell command and quoting can be lost. Do not combine this escaped-argument
form with shell operators such as `&&`; they would be literal arguments.

The job, state, staging, and working directory must remain available for queued
runs and retries. Ensure backend binaries and noninteractive authentication work
in the task environment; Ferry's own executable path does not fix the backend
`PATH`. Use distinguishable labels for additional batches. Keep this group's
parallelism at one unless you intentionally want concurrent **different** jobs
and have enough disk, relay capacity, and bandwidth.

## Inspect, verify, and retry

On the sender host:

```sh
pueue status
pueue log "$sender_id"
pueue follow "$sender_id"      # Ctrl-C detaches from the log view
ferry status /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender
```

Check delivery separately on the receiver host:

```sh
ferry status /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --json
journalctl --user -u ferry-mirror-receiver.service -f
```

Compare the expected units with the receiver's verified records and, when
appropriate, the destination contents. Status totals can include previous
batches; the sender's pushed count alone is not proof of receiver verification.

`pueue wait "$sender_id"` waits for a terminal task state; its exit status does
not distinguish task success from failure. Inspect `pueue status --json` or the
task log afterward. Even a successful Ferry exit is not an unconditional promise
that your intended batch arrived:

- `receive --once` scans the relay once; incomplete uploads or insufficient
  destination space can leave units behind without failing that pass.
- A sender can skip units that have not settled yet.
- Current SIGTERM handling can stop Ferry and return 0 with work still incomplete.

After diagnosing a failure, rerun the same job with the same persistent state.
Pueue can resubmit the command:

```sh
pueue restart "$sender_id"
```

By default this creates a new task ID, preserving the old result and log. Use
`pueue restart --in-place "$sender_id"` only when intentionally reusing the ID
and overwriting its previous log. Inspect whether the group is paused; resume
it deliberately with `pueue start --group ferry-send` if appropriate. Do not
submit another copy while the original sender is still running.

Do not delete ledgers, staging, relay protocol files, or destination partials to
force a retry. Pueue reruns the process; Ferry's state provides transfer resume.

## Dependencies and concurrency traps

**Do not make the receiver depend on the sender finishing.** `pueue add --after`
requires every dependency to succeed. With `after_receiver_ack`, the sender
waits for receiver verification before exiting; with relay backpressure, it may
need the receiver to free space before it can upload the remaining units.
Putting the receiver after the sender deadlocks those workflows. Putting both
in a shared one-slot group has the same problem.

Sequential send-then-receive is appropriate only for a small, static,
source-retaining batch that can fit entirely in the relay without waiting for
receiver activity. It is not the general recommendation. A one-pass receiver
still needs a separate completion check.

For repeated batches, prefer the continuously running receiver above. Ferry's
sender-done marker persists after a batch. A non-follow receiver started before
the next sender can see that old marker and an empty relay, then exit too early.
Do not delete protocol state as a scheduling workaround.

Ferry's per-side lock applies to the local state directory. A duplicate side
using that state exits 2; separate state directories or hosts do not share a
distributed lock. Pueue group limits also apply only to that daemon, so neither
mechanism makes duplicate cross-host senders safe.

## Remote hosts, reboot, and recurring schedules

Submit on the host that will execute the command. From another machine, SSH in
and run the Pueue client there, for example:

```sh
ssh sender-host 'pueue add --group ferry-send --label send-mirror-remote --escape -- /home/alex/.local/bin/ferry send /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml'
ssh sender-host 'pueue status'
```

Create the group and prepare that host's environment first. Pueue resolves the
submission working directory on the client: using a local client against a
remote daemon can pass a local-only or differently canonicalized path. Running
the client through SSH avoids that mismatch. Task IDs and dependencies belong
to one daemon; do not use a receiver host's task ID in a sender host's `--after`.

Pueue persists queue state, but it does not checkpoint a running Ferry process.
After a host reboot or daemon shutdown, inspect interrupted tasks and restart
them with the same Ferry state as needed. Automatic daemon startup depends on
your service-manager setup; configuring the queue is not itself boot setup.

Pueue's delay option is for a single delayed task, not a recurring calendar
schedule. Use [cron or a timer](operations.md#cron) for periodic runs, and a
service manager for long-lived `--follow` processes. Repeatedly adding tasks on
a timer can build an unbounded queue if a sender is still waiting, so do not
blindly enqueue a new batch on every tick.

import io
import threading
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from ferry import adapters, cli, core, proc, service, wizard
from ferry.job import job_from_dict, load_job
from ferry.receiver import receive
from ferry.sender import send


class Terminal(io.StringIO):
    def isatty(self):
        return True


def answers(tmp_path, *, backend="local", selection="glob", pack="tar", side="sender",
            method="manual", confirm="yes", extract="no", local_receiver="yes"):
    values = ["sample", str(tmp_path / "source"), str(tmp_path / "state"),
              str(tmp_path / "stage"), selection]
    if selection == "glob":
        values += ["*.txt"]
    else:
        values += ["_manifests/*.json", "data/{key}", "_manifests/{key}.json", ""]
    values += [pack, str(tmp_path / "destination")]
    if pack == "tar":
        values += [extract]
    values += [backend]
    values += {"local": [str(tmp_path / "relay")],
               "baidupcs": ["BaiduPCS-Go"],
               "rclone": ["gdrive:"],
               "ghrelease": ["owner/repository", "ferry-sample"],
               "rsync": ["nas", "/srv/landing", local_receiver]}[backend]
    values += ["/ferry/sample", side, method]
    if method == "cron":
        values += ["0 2 * * *"]
    return values + [confirm]


def invoke(tmp_path, values, *, to_stdout=False, target=None):
    target = target or tmp_path / "job.toml"
    stdin = Terminal("\n".join(values) + "\n")
    stdout, stderr = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    code = wizard.run(str(target), to_stdout=to_stdout, stdin=stdin, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr)
    return code, stdout.getvalue(), stderr.getvalue(), stdin


@pytest.fixture
def offline(monkeypatch):
    def forbidden(*args, **kwargs):
        pytest.fail("wizard/preview must not contact a backend or supervisor")

    for module, names in ((adapters, ("make_adapter",)),
                          (core, ("make_adapter", "adapter_for", "preflight")),
                          (cli, ("adapter_for", "preflight", "send", "receive")),
                          (proc, ("run", "run_transfer")),
                          (service, ("install_systemd", "install_cron", "uninstall_systemd",
                                     "uninstall_cron", "linger_enabled", "_systemctl")),
                          (service.subprocess, ("run", "Popen"))):
        for name in names:
            monkeypatch.setattr(module, name, forbidden)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["local", "baidupcs", "rclone", "ghrelease", "rsync"])
def test_backend_configs_are_valid_offline(tmp_path, offline, backend):
    code, stdout, stderr, stdin = invoke(tmp_path, answers(tmp_path, backend=backend))
    assert code == 0 and stdout == ""
    assert stdin.read() == ""
    job = load_job(tmp_path / "job.toml")
    assert job.remote.adapter == backend
    assert job.sender.delete_source == "never" and job.remote.egress == "direct"
    assert not job.receiver.extract
    assert "No transfer or service was started" in stderr
    if backend == "rsync":

    assert sorted(p.name for p in tmp_path.iterdir()) == ["job.toml"]

def test_failed_write_cleans_only_new_file(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    original = Path.open

    class FailedWrite:
        def __init__(self, stream):
            self.stream = stream

        def __enter__(self):
            return self

        def __exit__(self, *args):
            self.stream.close()

        def fileno(self):
            return self.stream.fileno()

        def write(self, text):
            self.stream.write(text[:10])
            self.stream.flush()
            raise OSError("disk full")

    def open_file(path, mode="r", *args, **kwargs):
        stream = original(path, mode, *args, **kwargs)
        return FailedWrite(stream) if mode == "x" else stream

    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, "open", open_file)
    code, _, stderr, _ = invoke(tmp_path, answers(tmp_path))
    assert code == 2 and "disk full" in stderr
    assert list(tmp_path.iterdir()) == []

    assert invoke(tmp_path, answers(tmp_path, pack="none"))[0] == 0
    job = load_job(tmp_path / "job.toml")
    stop = threading.Event()
    watchdog = threading.Timer(10, stop.set)
    watchdog.start()
    try:
        result = send(job, poll=0.01, stop=stop)
    finally:
        watchdog.cancel()
    assert result.pushed == 1 and not result.failed
    result = receive(job, once=True, poll=0.01)
    assert result.verified == 1 and not result.failed
    assert (tmp_path / "destination/hello.txt").read_bytes() == content
    assert (src / "hello.txt").read_bytes() == content

 ## Unattended operation
 
-Preview a supervisor definition before installing anything:
+Ferry has no daemon of its own. `--follow` runs a foreground loop; a supervisor
+keeps that process alive. The wizard can suggest a run method, but it never
+installs or starts one.
+
+| Need | Recommended owner |
+| --- | --- |
+| Continuously discover or receive units | systemd user service, or another service manager |
+| Queue a batch and detach from the terminal | [Pueue](pueue.md), with an independent receiver |
+| Run on a recurring calendar schedule | cron, or a manually managed timer |
+| Watch a foreground run interactively | a terminal or tmux; not automatic restart after reboot |
+
+Use **one owner for each job/side**. Do not run the same sender under both pueue
+and systemd, for example. A second process using the same state directory and
+side exits **2**; the lock prevents local overlap, not duplicate work across
+hosts or different state directories. Sender and receiver may run concurrently.
+Test manually with source retention before enabling unattended operation.
+
+### Environment and authentication
+
+Install Ferry and the required backend tools on each execution host. Use an
+absolute job filename and absolute filesystem paths in the job. Run the service
+as the same user whose backend login, SSH configuration, and persistent state
+it should use. Noninteractive SSH must work without password prompts.
+
+Supervisors do not necessarily load your interactive shell configuration.
+Generated entries locate the Ferry executable, but do not copy your interactive
+`PATH` for backend tools. Ensure `HOME` and the backend search path are correct.
+Use backend executable options where supported, or configure the supervisor's
+environment explicitly. Do not put authentication tokens or session contents in
+service definitions, job files, or log reports.
+
+### Systemd user service
+
+The following examples assume the job has `name = "mirror"`. Run them on the
+host that will execute the selected side, replacing paths as needed.
 
 ```sh
-ferry service job.toml --side receiver
-ferry service job.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
+# Preview only: no service changes or loginctl probe.
+ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver
+
+# Explicitly install, enable, and start receiving now.
+ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --install
+
+systemctl --user status ferry-mirror-receiver.service
+journalctl --user -u ferry-mirror-receiver.service -f
+
+# Stop, disable, and remove this generated unit.
+ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --uninstall
+```
+
+The unit lives under `~/.config/systemd/user/`, runs `receive --follow` (or
+`send --follow` for the sender side), and uses `Restart=on-failure` with a
+60-second restart delay. Installation can immediately begin transfers; inspect
+the job and preview first. For a continuously running sender, install its sender
+unit on the source host as well. For queued sender batches, do not install that
+sender unit; use the [pueue recipe](pueue.md) instead.
+
+For example, a user override created with
+`systemctl --user edit ferry-mirror-receiver.service` can set a reviewed backend
+search path:
+
+```ini
+[Service]
+Environment="PATH=/home/alex/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
+```
+
+Adjust it for the actual tool locations. Reload the user manager with
+`systemctl --user daemon-reload`, then deliberately restart the affected service
+to apply an environment change; restarting interrupts any current transfer.
+Keep the same job and state when resuming.
+
+User services need lingering to run independently of login sessions and start
+at boot. Installation reports the detected linger state; Ferry does not enable
+it. If host policy permits, explicitly run:
+
+```sh
+loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
+```
+
+This may require administrator approval. Some older or restricted hosts have no
+usable systemd user manager; do not assume `--user` or lingering is available.
+Use cron for periodic work or an available service manager for continuous work.
+A successful install is not a guarantee of connectivity after the next reboot.
+
+### Cron
+
+Preview first, then explicitly install the same job/side entry:
+
+```sh
+ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
+ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
+
+# Remove only Ferry's tagged entry for this job and side.
+ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender --kind cron --uninstall
 ```
 
-Systemd user units run follow mode with `Restart=on-failure`; cron uses one-shot
-commands and job locks prevent overlap. `--install` writes and enables the selected
-service, so it can start transfers immediately; `--uninstall` removes it. Systemd
-may need `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` to survive logout. On other supervisors,
-including launchd, use the corresponding send/receive command explicitly. Test
-manually with source retention before enabling any unattended destructive policy.
+Cron entries are tagged by job name and side; installing again replaces that
+entry and preserves unrelated entries. The sender runs without `--follow`; a
+receiver cron entry uses `receive --once`. `--once` means a single relay scan,
+not guaranteed batch completion: an unfinished upload or insufficient destination
+space can leave work behind. Cron provides periodic attempts, not a persistent
+receiver process.
+
+A non-follow sender can still wait indefinitely for retries, read windows,
+capacity, or receiver acknowledgements. Schedule or supervise the receiver
+independently when needed. Later cron invocations of an already-running side
+exit 2 rather than creating extra workers. The generated line discards process
+stdout/stderr; inspect `<state_dir>/sender.log` or `receiver.log` and the ledgers
+for transfer activity. Early startup errors may occur before those logs exist,
+so validate the command manually in the intended environment first.
+
+Cron often has a minimal `PATH`. Configure it through a reviewed crontab
+environment (which can affect other entries), and verify the host's cron timezone
+when choosing a schedule. Do not assume shell aliases, shell initialization, or
+an interactive SSH agent will be available.
+
+### Other supervisors
+
+Ferry does not install launchd jobs, systemd timers, or pueued. Use the appropriate
+service manager for a persistent `send --follow` or `receive --follow` process.
+For finite work, see [Pueue](pueue.md); persisting queue metadata is different
+from automatically resuming a process interrupted by a reboot.

````text
1	# Pueue
2	
3	[Pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) is an optional shell-task queue backed
4	by the `pueued` daemon. It can keep a submitted command running after you detach
5	from the terminal, label jobs, capture their output, and limit parallel tasks.
6	It is not a Ferry dependency, a distributed scheduler, or a replacement for
7	Ferry's integrity checks and resumable state.
8	
9	The examples use Pueue 4.0.2 command syntax. Install Pueue separately and manage
10	`pueued` with the execution host's service manager; consult the
11	[upstream documentation](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki) for setup.
12	Ferry does not install or start it. Run `pueue status` to confirm your intended
13	daemon is reachable before submitting anything.
14	
15	## Recommended arrangement
16	
17	- **Receiver host:** a service-managed `ferry receive ... --follow` keeps draining
18	  the relay, verifying units, and publishing acknowledgements when required.
19	- **Sender host:** Pueue queues non-follow `ferry send ...` batches in a dedicated
20	  group with controlled concurrency.
21	- **Each job/side has one owner:** do not also install a sender service for the
22	  same queued sender, or run a second receiver while its service is active.
23	
24	For continuous discovery on both sides, use service-managed `--follow` processes
25	instead of queue tasks expected to finish. Pueue groups limit the number of
26	whole Ferry processes, not Ferry's internal upload threads or parts.
27	
28	A non-follow sender is a batch command, **not a bounded-duration command**. It
29	can wait indefinitely for upload retries, source read windows, staging/relay
30	capacity, or receiver acknowledgements. An apparently stuck Running task needs
31	Ferry diagnostics, not necessarily another queued copy.
32	
33	## Prepare the receiver
34	
35	On the receiver host, review the generated job, backend access, destination,
36	and [service environment](operations.md#environment-and-authentication). The
37	examples assume `name = "mirror"` and host-appropriate copies of the job.
38	Start with `delete_source = "never"`.
39	
40	```sh
41	ferry doctor /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver
42	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver
43	# Explicitly install and start the receiver after reviewing the preview.
44	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --install
45	systemctl --user status ferry-mirror-receiver.service
46	```
47	
48	Doctor can contact the backend; it is not an offline validation command.
49	Installation starts receiving immediately. On hosts without a usable systemd
50	user manager, run the receiver under an available service manager, or in a
51	separate foreground terminal for a supervised trial. Do not put that receiver
52	behind the sender in a queue dependency chain.
53	
54	## Queue a sender batch
55	
56	On the sender host, first inspect source units and backend access:
57	
58	```sh
59	ferry doctor /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender
60	ferry plan /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml
61	```
62	
63	Create the dedicated group once. Pueue does not create missing groups when you
64	submit a task; if the group already exists, inspect it rather than recreating it.
65	
66	```sh
67	pueue group add ferry-send
68	pueue parallel 1 --group ferry-send
69	```
70	
71	Submit from a stable working directory, using absolute executable and job paths:
72	
73	```sh
74	cd "$HOME"
75	ferry_bin=$(command -v ferry)
76	job=/home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml
77	
78	sender_id=$(pueue add --group ferry-send --label send-mirror-batch01 \
79	  --print-task-id --escape -- "$ferry_bin" send "$job")
80	printf 'Sender task: %s\n' "$sender_id"
81	```
82	
83	Verify that `command -v ferry` returns an absolute executable path, not an alias
84	or shell function, before submitting. `--escape` preserves each argument,
85	including paths containing spaces. Without it, Pueue joins arguments into a
86	shell command and quoting can be lost. Do not combine this escaped-argument
87	form with shell operators such as `&&`; they would be literal arguments.
88	
89	The job, state, staging, and working directory must remain available for queued
90	runs and retries. Ensure backend binaries and noninteractive authentication work
91	in the task environment; Ferry's own executable path does not fix the backend
92	`PATH`. Use distinguishable labels for additional batches. Keep this group's
93	parallelism at one unless you intentionally want concurrent **different** jobs
94	and have enough disk, relay capacity, and bandwidth.
95	
96	## Inspect, verify, and retry
97	
98	On the sender host:
99	
100	```sh
101	pueue status
102	pueue log "$sender_id"
103	pueue follow "$sender_id"      # Ctrl-C detaches from the log view
104	ferry status /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender
105	```
106	
107	Check delivery separately on the receiver host:
108	
109	```sh
110	ferry status /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --json
111	journalctl --user -u ferry-mirror-receiver.service -f
112	```
113	
114	Compare the expected units with the receiver's verified records and, when
115	appropriate, the destination contents. Status totals can include previous
116	batches; the sender's pushed count alone is not proof of receiver verification.
117	
118	`pueue wait "$sender_id"` waits for a terminal task state; its exit status does
119	not distinguish task success from failure. Inspect `pueue status --json` or the
120	task log afterward. Even a successful Ferry exit is not an unconditional promise
121	that your intended batch arrived:
122	
123	- `receive --once` scans the relay once; incomplete uploads or insufficient
124	  destination space can leave units behind without failing that pass.
125	- A sender can skip units that have not settled yet.
126	- Current SIGTERM handling can stop Ferry and return 0 with work still incomplete.
127	
128	After diagnosing a failure, rerun the same job with the same persistent state.
129	Pueue can resubmit the command:
130	
131	```sh
132	pueue restart "$sender_id"
133	```
134	
135	By default this creates a new task ID, preserving the old result and log. Use
136	`pueue restart --in-place "$sender_id"` only when intentionally reusing the ID
137	and overwriting its previous log. Inspect whether the group is paused; resume
138	it deliberately with `pueue start --group ferry-send` if appropriate. Do not
139	submit another copy while the original sender is still running.
140	
141	Do not delete ledgers, staging, relay protocol files, or destination partials to
142	force a retry. Pueue reruns the process; Ferry's state provides transfer resume.
143	
144	## Dependencies and concurrency traps
145	
146	**Do not make the receiver depend on the sender finishing.** `pueue add --after`
147	requires every dependency to succeed. With `after_receiver_ack`, the sender
148	waits for receiver verification before exiting; with relay backpressure, it may
149	need the receiver to free space before it can upload the remaining units.
150	Putting the receiver after the sender deadlocks those workflows. Putting both
151	in a shared one-slot group has the same problem.
152	
153	Sequential send-then-receive is appropriate only for a small, static,
154	source-retaining batch that can fit entirely in the relay without waiting for
155	receiver activity. It is not the general recommendation. A one-pass receiver
156	still needs a separate completion check.
157	
158	For repeated batches, prefer the continuously running receiver above. Ferry's
159	sender-done marker persists after a batch. A non-follow receiver started before
160	the next sender can see that old marker and an empty relay, then exit too early.
161	Do not delete protocol state as a scheduling workaround.
162	
163	Ferry's per-side lock applies to the local state directory. A duplicate side
164	using that state exits 2; separate state directories or hosts do not share a
165	distributed lock. Pueue group limits also apply only to that daemon, so neither
166	mechanism makes duplicate cross-host senders safe.
167	
168	## Remote hosts, reboot, and recurring schedules
169	
170	Submit on the host that will execute the command. From another machine, SSH in
171	and run the Pueue client there, for example:
172	
173	```sh
174	ssh sender-host 'pueue add --group ferry-send --label send-mirror-remote --escape -- /home/alex/.local/bin/ferry send /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml'
175	ssh sender-host 'pueue status'
176	```
177	
178	Create the group and prepare that host's environment first. Pueue resolves the
179	submission working directory on the client: using a local client against a
180	remote daemon can pass a local-only or differently canonicalized path. Running
181	the client through SSH avoids that mismatch. Task IDs and dependencies belong
182	to one daemon; do not use a receiver host's task ID in a sender host's `--after`.
183	
184	Pueue persists queue state, but it does not checkpoint a running Ferry process.
185	After a host reboot or daemon shutdown, inspect interrupted tasks and restart
186	them with the same Ferry state as needed. Automatic daemon startup depends on
187	your service-manager setup; configuring the queue is not itself boot setup.
188	
189	Pueue's delay option is for a single delayed task, not a recurring calendar
190	schedule. Use [cron or a timer](operations.md#cron) for periodic runs, and a
191	service manager for long-lived `--follow` processes. Repeatedly adding tasks on
192	a timer can build an unbounded queue if a sender is still waiting, so do not
193	blindly enqueue a new batch on every tick.
194
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Operations
2	
3	## Inspect before transferring
4	
5	```sh
6	ferry doctor job.toml
7	ferry doctor job.toml --side receiver
8	ferry plan job.toml
9	ferry status job.toml
10	ferry status job.toml --side receiver --json
11	ferry status job.toml --scan-source --remote
12	```
13	
14	Doctor checks the selected backend and egress; it can contact remote services
15	and, for rsync, create a missing landing directory. It is not a generic dry-run
16	or proof that every later backend operation will succeed. Plan enumerates source
17	units and members; it does not simulate transfer, settling, or source deletion.
18	
19	Status normally reads local ledgers. `--scan-source` adds source enumeration;
20	`--remote` queries the backend for relay information. Sender and receiver have
21	separate state, so inspect each on its own host. Commands accept `--json`, but
22	service output remains supervisor text rather than a general JSON report.
23	
24	## Run and resume
25	
26	```sh
27	ferry send job.toml
28	ferry receive job.toml --once
29	```
30	
31	Send processes eligible work and marks the sender done. Receive with `--once`
32	makes one pass; without it, receive waits until the sender is done and the relay
33	is empty. For continuous operation, run `send --follow` and `receive --follow`
34	in separate processes, adding `--poll 60` to control idle polling in seconds.
35	
36	To resume, restart the same command with the same job, state, staging, and relay
37	prefix. Do not delete ledgers, staged manifests, or destination partial files to
38	"fix" an interrupted transfer. Uploaded parts with matching remote sizes can be
39	reused; downloaded parts are checked by SHA-256 before reuse. One sender and one
40	receiver may run per job on a host; a second instance of either side fails fast.
41	
42	Inspect `<state_dir>/sender.jsonl`, `receiver.jsonl`, and side logs when progress
43	stalls. Check read windows, settling, staging space, remote limits, destination
44	free space, and preflight errors. Keep credentials and session files out of reports.
45	
46	## Integrity and destination safety
47	
48	The sender hashes the packed payload and its parts. The receiver checks sizes,
49	part and whole-payload SHA-256 hashes, and tar member counts before recording
50	verification. It then removes that unit's relay data. With extraction enabled,
51	existing unit paths are replaced, including removal of files absent in the new copy.
52	
53	Change detection is weaker than transfer verification: its path-and-size
54	fingerprints miss same-size edits. `ferry inventory job.toml --no-upload --json`
55	previews fingerprints of an existing destination tree; omit `--no-upload` only
56	when you intend to publish them to the relay for sender-side skipping. Use
57	`--root PATH` for a source-shaped tree when `receiver.dest` contains a key template.
58	Inventory seeding is not a content-hash audit or evidence of a fresh transfer.
59	
60	## Source deletion
61	
62	- `never` is the default and the recommended starting point.
63	- `after_remote_size` deletes source members after upload size checks, **before
64	  destination SHA-256 verification**. Use only for independently recoverable data.
65	- `after_receiver_ack` waits for the receiver's verification acknowledgement.
66	  Keep the sender running or restart it to consume acknowledgements; one-shot
67	  sending can wait for the receiver rather than exiting immediately.
68	
69	Keep source units immutable throughout transfer and acknowledgement handling:
70	settling does not lock files, and deletion acts on source paths. Use trusted,
71	job-specific relay storage; do not fabricate acknowledgements or reuse old
72	protocol state for a different dataset. Neither deletion policy replaces backups.
73	
74	## Egress
75	
76	Backend subprocesses always have proxy environment variables stripped, including
77	when `egress = "any"`. The default `direct` policy rejects detected backend proxy
78	settings, fake-IP DNS in `198.18.0.0/15`, and routes through recognized tunnel
79	interfaces. Backend-internal proxy configuration and host routing still matter.
80	
81	Set `remote.egress = "any"`, or pass `--allow-proxy` to doctor/send/receive, only
82	when accepting those egress findings is intentional. This does not restore proxy
83	environment variables or fix missing authentication. `trusted_interfaces` exempts
84	interfaces you have independently verified route this backend directly. Host
85	checks cannot detect every transparent upstream proxy; verify cost-sensitive paths.
86	
87	## Unattended operation
88	
89	Ferry has no daemon of its own. `--follow` runs a foreground loop; a supervisor
90	keeps that process alive. The wizard can suggest a run method, but it never
91	installs or starts one.
92	
93	| Need | Recommended owner |
94	| --- | --- |
95	| Continuously discover or receive units | systemd user service, or another service manager |
96	| Queue a batch and detach from the terminal | [Pueue](pueue.md), with an independent receiver |
97	| Run on a recurring calendar schedule | cron, or a manually managed timer |
98	| Watch a foreground run interactively | a terminal or tmux; not automatic restart after reboot |
99	
100	Use **one owner for each job/side**. Do not run the same sender under both pueue
101	and systemd, for example. A second process using the same state directory and
102	side exits **2**; the lock prevents local overlap, not duplicate work across
103	hosts or different state directories. Sender and receiver may run concurrently.
104	Test manually with source retention before enabling unattended operation.
105	
106	### Environment and authentication
107	
108	Install Ferry and the required backend tools on each execution host. Use an
109	absolute job filename and absolute filesystem paths in the job. Run the service
110	as the same user whose backend login, SSH configuration, and persistent state
111	it should use. Noninteractive SSH must work without password prompts.
112	
113	Supervisors do not necessarily load your interactive shell configuration.
114	Generated entries locate the Ferry executable, but do not copy your interactive
115	`PATH` for backend tools. Ensure `HOME` and the backend search path are correct.
116	Use backend executable options where supported, or configure the supervisor's
117	environment explicitly. Do not put authentication tokens or session contents in
118	service definitions, job files, or log reports.
119	
120	### Systemd user service
121	
122	The following examples assume the job has `name = "mirror"`. Run them on the
123	host that will execute the selected side, replacing paths as needed.
124	
125	```sh
126	# Preview only: no service changes or loginctl probe.
127	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver
128	
129	# Explicitly install, enable, and start receiving now.
130	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --install
131	
132	systemctl --user status ferry-mirror-receiver.service
133	journalctl --user -u ferry-mirror-receiver.service -f
134	
135	# Stop, disable, and remove this generated unit.
136	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side receiver --uninstall
137	```
138	
139	The unit lives under `~/.config/systemd/user/`, runs `receive --follow` (or
140	`send --follow` for the sender side), and uses `Restart=on-failure` with a
141	60-second restart delay. Installation can immediately begin transfers; inspect
142	the job and preview first. For a continuously running sender, install its sender
143	unit on the source host as well. For queued sender batches, do not install that
144	sender unit; use the [pueue recipe](pueue.md) instead.
145	
146	For example, a user override created with
147	`systemctl --user edit ferry-mirror-receiver.service` can set a reviewed backend
148	search path:
149	
150	```ini
151	[Service]
152	Environment="PATH=/home/alex/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
153	```
154	
155	Adjust it for the actual tool locations. Reload the user manager with
156	`systemctl --user daemon-reload`, then deliberately restart the affected service
157	to apply an environment change; restarting interrupts any current transfer.
158	Keep the same job and state when resuming.
159	
160	User services need lingering to run independently of login sessions and start
161	at boot. Installation reports the detected linger state; Ferry does not enable
162	it. If host policy permits, explicitly run:
163	
164	```sh
165	loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
166	```
167	
168	This may require administrator approval. Some older or restricted hosts have no
169	usable systemd user manager; do not assume `--user` or lingering is available.
170	Use cron for periodic work or an available service manager for continuous work.
171	A successful install is not a guarantee of connectivity after the next reboot.
172	
173	### Cron
174	
175	Preview first, then explicitly install the same job/side entry:
176	
177	```sh
178	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *"
179	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender --kind cron --schedule "0 2 * * *" --install
180	
181	# Remove only Ferry's tagged entry for this job and side.
182	ferry service /home/alex/jobs/mirror.toml --side sender --kind cron --uninstall
183	```
184	
185	Cron entries are tagged by job name and side; installing again replaces that
186	entry and preserves unrelated entries. The sender runs without `--follow`; a
187	receiver cron entry uses `receive --once`. `--once` means a single relay scan,
188	not guaranteed batch completion: an unfinished upload or insufficient destination
189	space can leave work behind. Cron provides periodic attempts, not a persistent
190	receiver process.
191	
192	A non-follow sender can still wait indefinitely for retries, read windows,
193	capacity, or receiver acknowledgements. Schedule or supervise the receiver
194	independently when needed. Later cron invocations of an already-running side
195	exit 2 rather than creating extra workers. The generated line discards process
196	stdout/stderr; inspect `<state_dir>/sender.log` or `receiver.log` and the ledgers
197	for transfer activity. Early startup errors may occur before those logs exist,
198	so validate the command manually in the intended environment first.
199	
200	Cron often has a minimal `PATH`. Configure it through a reviewed crontab
201	environment (which can affect other entries), and verify the host's cron timezone
202	when choosing a schedule. Do not assume shell aliases, shell initialization, or
203	an interactive SSH agent will be available.
204	
205	### Other supervisors
206	
207	Ferry does not install launchd jobs, systemd timers, or pueued. Use the appropriate
208	service manager for a persistent `send --follow` or `receive --follow` process.
209	For finite work, see [Pueue](pueue.md); persisting queue metadata is different
210	from automatically resuming a process interrupted by a reboot.
211
````
